@@ -0,0 +1,115 @@
+# Sparse Disk
+
+The sparse disk backend moves sparse weight patches through storage instead of a
+trainer-to-inference NCCL group. While the engine serves, the trainer publishes
+each version's patches as one file. Every inference worker keeps its own part of
+the checkpoint in host memory, laid out as its load plan writes it. In the
+update, the worker applies the new files to that copy and copies the whole part
+into the model, so every update is a full direct reload through the load plan,
+with post-load processing rerun.
+
+Use it when the trainer and inference cannot share an NCCL group, or when many
+replicas pull the same update. Inside one NVLink domain, a dense NCCL update is
+usually faster. [ModelExpress](modelexpress.md) also installs deltas from object
+storage, through its own service; this backend needs only a shared directory.
+
+## Usage
+
+The inference side only selects the backend; `VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1` exposes
+the HTTP weight-transfer endpoints:
+
+```bash
+VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 vllm serve my-model \
+    --weight-transfer-config '{"backend": "sparse_disk"}'
+```
+
+The trainer passes patches in checkpoint coordinates, as for
+[sparse NCCL](nccl.md#sparse-nccl), with strictly increasing indices per tensor:
+
+```python
+from vllm.distributed.weight_transfer import (
+    HTTPVLLMWeightSyncClient,
+    WeightTransferTrainerFactory,
+)
+from vllm.distributed.weight_transfer.sparse_disk_engine import (
+    SparseDiskTrainerInitInfo,
+)
+
+engine = WeightTransferTrainerFactory.trainer_init(
+    SparseDiskTrainerInitInfo(
+        patch_dir="/shared/run-42/patches",   # every inference host reads this path
+        rank=0,
+    ),
+    client=HTTPVLLMWeightSyncClient("http://localhost:8000"),
+)
+engine.send_weights()     # once, before serving: builds the host copies
+
+engine.publish(patches)   # while the engine serves
+engine.send_weights()     # between /pause and /resume: apply the version and reload
+```
+
+`publish` writes the next version (1, 2, ...) with `save_sparse_patches`;
+`send_weights` runs start, update and finish for the last published version. An
+orchestrator that publishes files itself can call `save_sparse_patches(patches,
+patch_dir, version)` and drive the client with `{"version": version}`.
+
+## Storage and the host copy
+
+- **Patch files.** `patch_file(patch_dir, version)`, named
+  `patch-<version, 12 digits>.safetensors`, holds the changes from
+  `version - 1`; write it with `save_sparse_patches`. Versions are consecutive
+  and each is written once, in place and without a rename, as object-store
+  mounts need. A file is read only in the update, so place it on the inference
+  host (or in its page cache) before the pause.
+- **Base checkpoint.** Version `base_version` is the checkpoint the servers
+  started from, and the first file holds the changes from exactly that
+  checkpoint; nothing checks this, and nothing checks the weights after an
+  update either. A trainer that restarts needs a new `patch_dir`, and servers
+  restarted from the checkpoint it resumes from.
+- **Host copy.** The first update builds the load plan, as dense NCCL with
+  `use_load_plan` does, and copies every part of the startup checkpoint the
+  worker loads into host memory, pinned where available: about the checkpoint
+  size divided by the tensor-parallel size per worker, for every server. That
+  update also reads the checkpoint, so send it before serving (the
+  `send_weights()` above, at `base_version`). Later updates apply the new files
+  and copy the worker's part into the model. Applying maps the patch on the
+  worker's device, in chunks sized to its free memory. Pinned host memory cannot
+  be swapped or reclaimed; a tensor that is not sharded, or that the load plan
+  leaves to `load_weights`, is held whole by every worker.
+- **Names.** Patches name checkpoint tensors, as the default loader yields
+  them. A patch of a tensor the model does not load, such as a tied alias, is
+  checked and ignored.
+
+## Versions and Recovery
+
+- A server that starts later, or restarts, serves its startup checkpoint until
+  it is initialized and updated: send it `init_weight_transfer_engine` with
+  `patch_dir` and its checkpoint's `base_version`, then update it to
+  `{"version": <current>}`. That update builds the copy and replays every file
+  after `base_version`, so its time grows with the number of versions: save a
+  full checkpoint every so often and start new servers from it. A server keeps
+  the `base_version` of its first init.
+- Sending the last update again reloads the copy, for example after a failed
+  update or a level 2 sleep.
+- Every worker checks the whole file before writing any of it, so a file with a
+  bad patch is refused by every worker, with an error naming the file, and
+  leaves every copy at the last version. Only such a file may be corrected
+  under the same version: delete it and write it again with
+  `save_sparse_patches`; after any other failed update, keep the file. Either
+  way the model stays mid-update, so keep generation paused and send an update
+  that succeeds. On tensor-parallel servers, restart the server first: the next
+  request currently gets the failed update's error back. An apply that fails
+  partway discards the copy, which the next update rebuilds.
+- Versions only move forward. To go back, restart the servers from a full
+  checkpoint and use a new `patch_dir`.
+
+## Limitations
+
+- Needs the default loader reading the checkpoint on the host (not
+  `fastsafetensors` or `instanttensor`), no secondary weight sources, and a load
+  plan: direct reload, without EPLB or online quantization. Other
+  configurations are refused at `init_weight_transfer_engine`; a model whose
+  loads cannot be planned fails at the first update.
+- Draft model weights are not updated.
+- The host copy takes host memory for every server, pinned where available, and
+  is rebuilt after a restart.

+    save_torch_state_dict(dict(weights), folder, max_shard_size=80)
+    assert len(list(folder.glob("model-*-of-00002.safetensors"))) == 2
+    assert (folder / "model.safetensors.index.json").exists()

+def _read_sparse_disk_checkpoint(folder):
+    weights: dict[str, torch.Tensor] = {}
+    for file in sorted(folder.glob("*.safetensors")):
+        weights |= safetensors.torch.load_file(file)
+    return weights

+def _sparse_disk_model(weights):
+    """A model cold-started on `weights` whose loaders take the halves a second
+    tensor-parallel rank takes ("rows" along dim 0, "cols" along dim 1), split
+    "split" along dim 1 over two parameters and double "a" in place, which a load
+    plan leaves to `load_weights`; it skips "unused"."""
+    from vllm.model_executor.model_loader.reload.direct import track_loaded_params
+    from vllm.model_executor.model_loader.utils import process_weights_after_loading
+
+    loaders = {
+        "a": lambda p, w: p.copy_(w.mul_(2)),  # changes its input
+        "rows": lambda p, w: p.copy_(w[2:]),
+        "cols": lambda p, w: p.copy_(w[:, 2:]),
+    }
+    shapes = {"rows": (2, 4), "cols": (4, 2)}
+    model = torch.nn.Module()
+    params = {n: (t.shape, t.dtype) for n, t in _SPARSE_DISK_BASE.items()}
+    params |= dict.fromkeys(("split_lo", "split_hi"), ((2, 2), torch.bfloat16))
+    for name, (shape, dtype) in params.items():
+        if name in ("unused", "split"):
+            continue
+        p = torch.nn.Parameter(
+            torch.zeros(shapes.get(name, shape), dtype=dtype), requires_grad=False
+        )
+        p.weight_loader = loaders.get(name, lambda p, w: p.copy_(w))
+        model.register_parameter(name, p)
+
+    def load_weights(weights):
+        params = dict(model.named_parameters())
+        loaded = set()
+        for name, w in weights:
+            if name == "split":
+                params["split_lo"].copy_(w[:, :2])
+                params["split_hi"].copy_(w[:, 2:])
+                loaded |= {"split_lo", "split_hi"}
+            elif name in params:
+                params[name].weight_loader(params[name], w)
+                loaded.add(name)
+        return loaded
+
+    model.load_weights = load_weights
+    track_loaded_params(model)  # as a direct-mode cold start does
+    model.load_weights(weights.items())
+    process_weights_after_loading(model, _SPARSE_DISK_MODEL_CONFIG, torch.device("cpu"))
+    return model
+

+def _bits(model):
+    return {
+        n: p.data.reshape(-1).view(torch.uint8).tolist()
+        for n, p in model.named_parameters()
+    }
+

+def _dense_patch(weights, versions):
+    """The weights after writing every patch of `versions`, in order."""
+    weights = {name: t.clone() for name, t in weights.items()}
+    for patches in versions:
+        for patch in patches:
+            weights[patch.name].view(-1)[patch.indices.long()] = patch.values
+    return weights

+"""Sparse disk weight transfer engine.
+
+The trainer publishes each version's sparse patches as one file on storage that
+every inference host can read, while the engine serves. Each worker keeps its
+part of the checkpoint in host memory, as its load plan writes it; in the update
+it applies the new files there and copies that whole part into the model.
+"""

+logger = init_logger(__name__)

+    "SparseDiskTrainerWeightTransferEngine",
+    "SparseDiskWeightTransferEngine",
+    "SparseDiskWeightTransferInitInfo",
+    "SparseDiskWeightTransferUpdateInfo",
+    "patch_file",
+    "save_sparse_patches",
+]
+
+_FORMAT = "sparse_disk/1"
+# Same-size integer views, so patches are copied bit for bit whatever the dtype.
+_INT_VIEWS = {1: torch.int8, 2: torch.int16, 4: torch.int32, 8: torch.int64}
+# Most patch elements mapped to the host copy at a time.
+_APPLY_CHUNK = 1 << 24
+
+
+def _numel(box: "Box") -> int:
+    return math.prod(b - a for a, b in box)
+
+
+def patch_file(patch_dir: str | Path, version: int) -> Path:
+    """The file that holds `version`'s patches."""
+    return Path(patch_dir) / f"patch-{version:012d}.safetensors"
+
+
+def save_sparse_patches(
+    patches: Iterable[SparseWeightPatch], patch_dir: str | Path, version: int
+) -> Path:
+    """Write `version`'s patches, the changes from `version - 1`, to `patch_dir`.
+
+    Patch values overwrite the checkpoint values at their flat indices, which
+    must be strictly increasing; a tensor is patched at most once per version.
+    Patches with values of one dtype are stored as one concatenated index and
+    value tensor. A version is written once: publishing it again raises.
+    """
+    groups: dict[torch.dtype, list[SparseWeightPatch]] = {}
+    names: set[str] = set()
+    for patch in patches:
+        indices = patch.indices
+        if indices.dtype not in (torch.int32, torch.int64):
+            raise ValueError(f"indices of {patch.name} must be int32 or int64")
+        if indices.ndim != 1 or indices.shape != patch.values.shape:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"indices and values of {patch.name} must be 1-D and the same length"
+            )
+        if indices.numel() and not (
+            bool((indices[1:] > indices[:-1]).all())
+            and int(indices[0]) >= 0
+            and int(indices[-1]) < math.prod(patch.full_shape)
+        ):
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"indices of {patch.name} must be strictly increasing and in range"
+            )
+        if patch.name in names:
+            raise ValueError(f"{patch.name} is patched twice")
+        names.add(patch.name)
+        groups.setdefault(patch.values.dtype, []).append(patch)
+    tensors: dict[str, torch.Tensor] = {}
+    entries = []
+    for i, group in enumerate(groups.values()):
+        wide = any(math.prod(p.full_shape) > 2**31 for p in group)
+        index_dtype = torch.int64 if wide else torch.int32
+        tensors[f"{i}.indices"] = torch.cat(
+            [p.indices.detach().cpu().to(index_dtype) for p in group]
+        )
+        tensors[f"{i}.values"] = torch.cat([p.values.detach().cpu() for p in group])
+        entries += [
+            {
+                "name": p.name,
+                "shape": list(p.full_shape),
+                "group": i,
+                "count": p.indices.numel(),
+            }
+            for p in group
+        ]
+    data = save(tensors, {"format": _FORMAT, "patches": json.dumps(entries)})
+    # Created exclusively and written in place, as `save_file` may rename a
+    # temporary file, which object-store mounts cannot do; opened outside the
+    # try, so a published version is never removed. A version is applied only
+    # after this returns, and a file cut short by a crash fails to open.
+    path = patch_file(patch_dir, version)
+    f = open(path, "xb")  # noqa: SIM115
+    try:
+        with f:
+            f.write(data)
+    except BaseException:
+        with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
+            path.unlink()
+        raise
+    return path

+    patch_dir: str

+    inference host."""

+    """Version of the checkpoint the inference servers started from."""

+    """Update info for the sparse disk backend."""

+class SparseDiskWeightTransferEngine(
+    WeightTransferEngine[

+    ]

+    the checkpoint, then loads that whole part into the model.
+
+    The first update builds the copy from the startup checkpoint, at
+    `base_version`, and replays the files after it; a restarted server does the
+    same. The copy holds what the load plan writes on this worker, in pinned
+    memory where available.
+    """
+
+    init_info_cls = SparseDiskWeightTransferInitInfo
+    update_info_cls = SparseDiskWeightTransferUpdateInfo
+    supports_draft_weight_update = False

+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        config: WeightTransferConfig,
+        vllm_config: "VllmConfig",
+        device: torch.device,
+        model: torch.nn.Module,
+    ) -> None:
+        super().__init__(config, vllm_config, device, model)
+        self._init_info: SparseDiskWeightTransferInitInfo | None = None
+        self._copy: _HostCopy | None = None
+        # The version the model holds; it outlives the copy.
+        self._loaded = 0
+
+    def init_transfer_engine(self, init_info: SparseDiskWeightTransferInitInfo) -> None:
+        """Check that the model can load through a load plan from its startup
+        checkpoint files."""
+        from vllm.model_executor.model_loader import get_model_loader
+        from vllm.model_executor.model_loader.default_loader import (
+            DefaultModelLoader,
+        )
+        from vllm.model_executor.model_loader.reload import check_plannable

+        load_format = self.vllm_config.load_config.load_format
+        loader = get_model_loader(self.vllm_config.load_config)
+        if type(loader) is not DefaultModelLoader or load_format in (
+            "fastsafetensors",
+            "instanttensor",
+        ):
+            raise ValueError(
+                "sparse_disk builds its copy from the checkpoint files on the host "
+                f"and needs the default loader, not load_format={load_format!r}"
+            )
+        if self._init_info is None:
+            self._loaded = init_info.base_version
+        elif init_info.base_version != self._init_info.base_version:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"this server started from version {self._init_info.base_version}, "
+                f"not {init_info.base_version}; restart it from that checkpoint"
+            )
+        if getattr(self.model, "secondary_weights", ()):
+            raise ValueError("sparse_disk does not support secondary weight sources")

+        self.shutdown()
+        self._init_info = init_info
+
+    def start_weight_update(self) -> None:
+        from vllm.model_executor.model_loader.reload import start_reload
+
+        start_reload(self.model)
+
+    def finish_weight_update(self) -> None:
+        from vllm.model_executor.model_loader.reload import finish_reload
+
+        finish_reload(self.model, self.model_config, self.device)
+
+    def receive_weights(self, update_info: SparseDiskWeightTransferUpdateInfo) -> None:
+        """Bring the host copy to the version, then load it into the model."""
+        init_info = self._init_info
+        if init_info is None:
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                "Sparse disk weight transfer engine not initialized. "
+                "Call init_transfer_engine() first."
+            )
+        newest = max(self._loaded, self._copy.version if self._copy else 0)
+        if update_info.version < newest:
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                f"this server has applied version {newest}, newer than "
+                f"{update_info.version}; versions only move forward"
+            )
+        if self._copy is None:
+            self._copy = _HostCopy(self, init_info.base_version)
+        copy = self._copy
+        with set_default_torch_num_threads():
+            while copy.version < update_info.version:
+                path = patch_file(init_info.patch_dir, copy.version + 1)
+                started = time.perf_counter()
+                try:
+                    with safe_open(path, framework="pt") as f:
+                        writes = copy.map(f)
+                except (ValueError, SafetensorError) as e:
+                    raise ValueError(f"{path}: {e}") from e
+                try:
+                    for dtype, positions, values in writes:  # bit for bit
+                        copy.buffers[dtype].view(values.dtype)[positions] = values
+                except BaseException:
+                    self.shutdown()  # partly written: rebuilt at the next update
+                    raise
+                del writes  # before the next file is mapped
+                copy.version += 1
+                logger.info("Applied %s in %.2f s", path, time.perf_counter() - started)
+        if self.device.type != "cpu":
+            torch.accelerator.empty_cache()  # the mapping's temporaries
+        copy.load(self.model)
+        self._loaded = copy.version
+
+    def shutdown(self) -> None:
+        from vllm.v1.kv_offload.cpu.host_register import host_unregister
+
+        for ptr in self._copy.registered if self._copy else ():
+            host_unregister(ptr)
+        self._copy = None

+class _HostCopy:
+    """A worker's part of the checkpoint at `version`, as its load plan writes
+    it: per checkpoint dtype, one host buffer of every box this worker loads.
+    A name the plan leaves to `load_weights` holds its whole tensor there."""

+        from vllm.model_executor.model_loader.reload import plan_loads
+        from vllm.utils.platform_utils import is_pin_memory_available
+        from vllm.v1.kv_offload.cpu.host_register import host_register
+
+        started = time.perf_counter()
+        self.version = version
+        self.device = device = engine.device
+        model, model_config = engine.model, engine.model_config
+        loader = get_model_loader(engine.vllm_config.load_config)
+        # what the default loader feeds the model, as at the cold start
+        meta = [
+            ParamMeta(n, t.dtype, tuple(t.shape))
+            for n, t in loader.get_all_weights(model_config, model)
+        ]
+        # every one of them, to check patch files against
+        self.catalog = {m.name: (m.shape, m.dtype) for m in meta}
+        self.plan = plan_loads(model, meta)
+        # name -> [(box, offset into its dtype's buffer)]
+        self.parts: dict[str, list[tuple[Box, int]]] = {}
+        sizes: dict[torch.dtype, int] = {}
+        for m in meta:
+            for box in self.plan.get_boxes(m.name) or ():
+                offset = sizes.get(m.dtype, 0)
+                self.parts.setdefault(m.name, []).append((box, offset))
+                sizes[m.dtype] = offset + _numel(box)
+        self.fallbacks = [m.name for m in meta if self.plan.get_dest(m.name) is None]
+        self.buffers = {d: torch.empty(n, dtype=d) for d, n in sizes.items()}
+        with set_default_torch_num_threads():
+            for name, t in loader.get_all_weights(model_config, model):
+                for box, flat in self._views(name):
+                    part = t[tuple(slice(a, b) for a, b in box)]
+                    flat.view(part.shape).copy_(part)
+        self.pairs = [
+            (dst, dict(self._views(name))[box].view(dst.shape))
+            for name in self.parts
+            for box, dst in self.plan.get_dest(name) or ()
+        ]
+        self._index_geometry()
+        # last, so that a failure above leaves no registration behind
+        pin = device.type != "cpu" and is_pin_memory_available()
+        self.registered = [
+            b.data_ptr()
+            for b in self.buffers.values()
+            if pin and host_register(b.data_ptr(), b.nbytes)
+        ]
+        logger.info(
+            "Built the host copy of %d tensors (%.2f GiB, %s) in %.1f s",
+            len(meta),
+            sum(b.nbytes for b in self.buffers.values()) / 2**30,
+            "pinned" if self.registered else "pageable",
+            time.perf_counter() - started,
+        )
+
+    def _views(self, name: str) -> list[tuple["Box", torch.Tensor]]:
+        parts = self.parts.get(name, ())
+        flat = self.buffers[self.catalog[name][1]] if parts else None
+        return [(box, flat[o : o + _numel(box)]) for box, o in parts]  # type: ignore[index]
+
+    def _index_geometry(self) -> None:
+        """Device tensors to map patch elements in bulk: per checkpoint name,
+        its shape and, per slot, one of its boxes on this worker with its copy
+        offset; slots past its last box are empty."""
+        self.ids = {name: i for i, name in enumerate(self.catalog)}
+        ndim = max([1, *(len(shape) for shape, _ in self.catalog.values())])
+        slots = max([1, *map(len, self.parts.values())])
+        shapes, boxes, bases = [], [], []
+        for name, (shape, _) in self.catalog.items():
+            parts = [
+                ([(0, 1)] * (ndim - len(box)) + list(box), offset)
+                for box, offset in self.parts.get(name, ())
+            ]
+            parts += [([(0, 0)] * ndim, 0)] * (slots - len(parts))
+            shapes.append([1] * (ndim - len(shape)) + list(shape))
+            boxes.append([box for box, _ in parts])
+            bases.append([offset for _, offset in parts])
+        box = torch.tensor(boxes, dtype=torch.long, device=self.device)
+        self.geometry = (
+            torch.tensor(shapes, dtype=torch.long, device=self.device).T,
+            box[..., 0].permute(1, 2, 0),
+            box[..., 1].permute(1, 2, 0),
+            torch.tensor(bases, dtype=torch.long, device=self.device).T,
+        )
+
+    def map(self, f: Any) -> list[tuple[torch.dtype, torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]]:
+        """Check every patch of the open file `f` against the checkpoint and
+        find where its values land in this copy, without touching it: (buffer
+        dtype, positions in it, values as same-size integers)."""
+        metadata = f.metadata() or {}
+        if metadata.get("format") != _FORMAT:
+            raise ValueError(f"not a {_FORMAT} patch file")
+        entries = json.loads(metadata["patches"])
+        if len({e["name"] for e in entries}) != len(entries):
+            raise ValueError("a tensor is patched twice")
+        writes = []
+        for i in sorted({e["group"] for e in entries}):
+            group = [e for e in entries if e["group"] == i]
+            indices = f.get_tensor(f"{i}.indices")
+            values = f.get_tensor(f"{i}.values")
+            for e in group:
+                if e["name"] not in self.catalog:
+                    raise ValueError(f"{e['name']} is not in the checkpoint")
+                if (tuple(e["shape"]), values.dtype) != self.catalog[e["name"]]:
+                    raise ValueError(
+                        f"{e['name']} is {e['shape']} {values.dtype}, "
+                        f"the checkpoint {self.catalog[e['name']]}"
+                    )
+            counts = torch.tensor([e["count"] for e in group])
+            if (
+                counts.dtype != torch.int64
+                or indices.dtype not in (torch.int32, torch.int64)
+                or (counts < 0).any()
+                or not indices.shape == values.shape == (int(counts.sum()),)
+            ):
+                raise ValueError(f"bad group {i}")
+            names = [e["name"] for e in group]
+            values = values.view(_INT_VIEWS[values.element_size()])
+            for positions, src in self._map_bulk(names, counts, indices, values):
+                writes.append((self.catalog[names[0]][1], positions, src))
+        return writes
+
+    def _map_bulk(
+        self,
+        names: list[str],
+        counts: torch.Tensor,
+        indices: torch.Tensor,
+        values: torch.Tensor,
+    ) -> Iterable[tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]]:
+        """Check and map every element, a chunk at a time on the worker's
+        device, and yield the copy offset and value of each one in a box."""
+        ids = torch.tensor([self.ids[n] for n in names], device=self.device)
+        size, start, stop, base = (t[..., ids] for t in self.geometry)
+        numel = size.prod(0)
+        slots = [len(self.parts.get(n, ())) for n in names]
+        boxes = torch.tensor(slots, device=self.device)
+        ends = counts.cumsum(0)
+        ends_list = ends.tolist()
+        chunk = _chunk_elements(self.device)
+        for lo in range(0, indices.numel(), chunk):
+            hi = min(lo + chunk, indices.numel())
+            first = max(lo - 1, 0)  # with the last element before, for the order
+            a = bisect.bisect_right(ends_list, first)
+            b = bisect.bisect_left(ends_list, hi) + 1
+            span = ends[a:b].clamp(max=hi) - (ends[a:b] - counts[a:b]).clamp(min=first)
+            k = torch.repeat_interleave(
+                torch.arange(a, b, device=self.device),
+                span.to(self.device),
+                output_size=hi - first,
+            )
+            index = indices[first:hi].to(self.device).long()
+            falling = (k[1:] == k[:-1]) & (index[1:] <= index[:-1])
+            bad = torch.cat([k[1:][falling], k[(index < 0) | (index >= numel[k])]])
+            if bad.numel():
+                raise ValueError(f"bad indices for {names[int(bad.min())]}")
+            k, index = k[lo - first :], index[lo - first :]
+            src = values[lo:hi].to(self.device)
+            for s in range(max(slots)):
+                if s:  # only the names with a box in this slot
+                    more = (boxes[k] > s).nonzero().view(-1)
+                    k, index, src = k[more], index[more], src[more]
+                rest = index
+                selected = torch.ones_like(index, dtype=torch.bool)
+                position = base[s, k]
+                stride = torch.ones_like(index)
+                for d in reversed(range(size.shape[0])):
+                    extent = size[d, k]
+                    coord = rest % extent
+                    rest = rest // extent
+                    a_d, b_d = start[s, d, k], stop[s, d, k]
+                    selected &= (coord >= a_d) & (coord < b_d)
+                    position += (coord - a_d) * stride
+                    stride *= b_d - a_d
+                chosen = selected.nonzero().view(-1)
+                yield position[chosen].cpu(), src[chosen].cpu()
+
+    def load(self, model: torch.nn.Module) -> None:
+        """Copy the whole part into the model and report it loaded."""
+        from vllm.model_executor.model_loader.reload.direct import mark_loaded
+
+        for dst, src in self.pairs:
+            dst.copy_(src, non_blocking=src.dtype == dst.dtype)
+        for name in self.parts:
+            for w in self.plan.entries[name].writes or ():
+                mark_loaded(model, f"{w.module}.{w.tensor}" if w.module else w.tensor)
+        if self.fallbacks:
+            model.load_weights(
+                [
+                    (n, self._views(n)[0][1].view(self.catalog[n][0]).clone())
+                    for n in self.fallbacks
+                ]
+            )
+
+
+def _chunk_elements(device: torch.device) -> int:
+    """Patch elements to map at once: about 200 bytes each of free device
+    memory, within bounds."""
+    from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+    if device.type == "cpu":
+        return _APPLY_CHUNK
+    free = current_platform.free_device_memory(device)
+    free += torch.accelerator.memory_reserved(device)
+    free -= torch.accelerator.memory_allocated(device)
+    return max(1 << 20, min(_APPLY_CHUNK, free // 200))
+
+
+@dataclass
+class SparseDiskTrainerInitInfo(TrainerInitInfo):
+    """Trainer-side init info for the sparse disk backend; the sender ships the
+    worker-side fields at the handshake."""
+
+    backend: ClassVar[str] = "sparse_disk"
+
+    patch_dir: str
+    """Directory to publish patch files to; every inference host must read it at
+    the same path."""
+    base_version: int = 0
+    """Version of the checkpoint the inference servers started from; the first
+    `publish` writes the next one."""
+
+
+class SparseDiskTrainerWeightTransferEngine(
+    TrainerWeightTransferEngine[SparseDiskTrainerInitInfo]
+):
+    """Trainer-side sparse disk weight transfer engine.
+
+    `publish(patches)` writes the next version while the engine serves;
+    `send_weights()`, called in the pause, updates the inference side to it.
+    Patches are in checkpoint coordinates, as for sparse NCCL, and only the
+    sender's are published.
+    """
+
+    init_info_cls = SparseDiskTrainerInitInfo
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        *,
+        client: VLLMWeightSyncClient,
+        patch_dir: str,
+        version: int,
+        source: WeightSource | None = None,
+        is_sender: bool = True,
+    ) -> None:
+        if source is not None:
+            raise ValueError(
+                "Sparse disk weight transfer takes no WeightSource; pass each "
+                "round's patches to publish(patches) instead."
+            )
+        super().__init__(client=client, source=source, is_sender=is_sender)
+        self.patch_dir = patch_dir
+        # The last version published.
+        self.version = version
+
+    @classmethod
+    def trainer_init(
+        cls,
+        init_info: SparseDiskTrainerInitInfo,
+        *,
+        client: VLLMWeightSyncClient,
+        source: WeightSource | None = None,
+    ) -> Self:
+        engine = cls(
+            client=client,
+            patch_dir=init_info.patch_dir,
+            version=init_info.base_version,
+            source=source,
+            is_sender=init_info.is_sender,
+        )
+        if engine.is_sender:
+            client.init_weight_transfer_engine(
+                {"patch_dir": engine.patch_dir, "base_version": engine.version}
+            )
+        return engine
+
+    def publish(self, patches: Iterable[SparseWeightPatch]) -> None:
+        """Write the next version's patches."""
+        if self.is_sender:
+            save_sparse_patches(patches, self.patch_dir, self.version + 1)
+            self.version += 1
+
+    def send_weights(self) -> None:
+        """Update the inference side to the last published version."""
+        if not self.is_sender:
+            return
+        self.client.start_weight_update()
+        self.client.update_weights({"version": self.version})
+        self.client.finish_weight_update()

Signed-off-by: Effi Ofer <effi.ofer@gmail.com>

@@ -7,12 +7,13 @@ This guide covers configuration of the [`OffloadingConnector`](disagg_prefill.md
 
 ## Overview
 
-Two specs are available, selected by the `spec_name` key in `kv_connector_extra_config`:
+Three specs are available, selected by the `spec_name` key in `kv_connector_extra_config`:
 
 - `CPUOffloadingSpec` (default): single CPU tier. Completed GPU blocks are copied into pinned host memory.
 - `TieringOffloadingSpec`: multi-tier. A CPU primary tier plus one or more secondary tiers.
+- `FSOffloadingSpec`: single file tier with direct GPU access. Blocks move between GPU memory and files without staging through host memory. See [Direct Storage Setup](#direct-storage-setup).
 
-Only the CPU primary tier has direct GPU access. Secondary tiers cannot read from or write to GPU memory; all GPU↔secondary transfers are staged through the CPU primary tier.
+Within `TieringOffloadingSpec`, only the CPU primary tier has direct GPU access. Secondary tiers cannot read from or write to GPU memory; all GPU↔secondary transfers are staged through the CPU primary tier.
 
 ```mermaid
 flowchart LR
@@ -109,12 +110,37 @@ vllm serve <model> \
 
 Secondary tiers are not supported yet on engines whose workers span several nodes; such an engine fails at startup.
 
+## Direct Storage Setup
+
+Set `spec_name` to `"FSOffloadingSpec"` to transfer blocks directly between GPU memory and files under `root_dir`. The worker backend is selected by `fs_backend`; the only backend is `gds`, which uses NVIDIA GPUDirect Storage (cuFile) and requires an NVIDIA GPU, `libcufile`, and a GDS-capable filesystem.
+
+```bash
+vllm serve <model> \
+  --kv-transfer-config '{
+    "kv_connector": "OffloadingConnector",
+    "kv_role": "kv_both",
+    "kv_connector_extra_config": {
+      "spec_name": "FSOffloadingSpec",
+      "fs_backend": "gds",
+      "root_dir": "/mnt/nvme/kv_cache",
+      "block_size": 64
+    }
+  }'
+```
+
+Files are named by block content hash, so blocks written by an earlier run or by another instance with the same model and parallel configuration are found by an asynchronous on-disk lookup. Set `access_mode` to `read` for an instance that only loads files written elsewhere and never writes; the default, `readwrite`, also stores the blocks it computes. Keys found on disk are remembered in an in-memory LRU index of `fs_index_size` entries so later requests skip the disk lookup; dropping a key from the index does not delete its file.
+
 ## `kv_connector_extra_config` Reference
 
 | Key | Required | Default | Scope | Notes |
 | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
-| `spec_name` | no | `CPUOffloadingSpec` | both | Set to `TieringOffloadingSpec` for multi-tier. |
-| `cpu_bytes_to_use` | yes | — | both | Total bytes of host memory reserved for the CPU tier across all workers (not per-worker). |
+| `spec_name` | no | `CPUOffloadingSpec` | both | Set to `TieringOffloadingSpec` for multi-tier, or `FSOffloadingSpec` for direct storage. |
+| `cpu_bytes_to_use` | yes | — | both | Total bytes of host memory reserved for the CPU tier across all workers (not per-worker). Not used by `FSOffloadingSpec`. |

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Tests for FSOffloadingManager's index, in-flight store tracking and disk
+lookups."""
+
+import os
+import time
+from collections.abc import Iterator
+
+import pytest
+
+from vllm.v1.kv_offload.base import (
+    LookupResult,
+    OffloadKey,
+    ReqContext,
+    ScheduleEndContext,
+    StoreTrigger,
+    make_offload_key,
+)
+from vllm.v1.kv_offload.file_mapper import FileMapper
+from vllm.v1.kv_offload.fs.manager import FSOffloadingManager
+
+_CTX = ReqContext(req_id="r1")
+_STEP_END = ScheduleEndContext(new_req_ids=(), preempted_req_ids=())
+_TRIGGER = StoreTrigger.ON_COMPUTE
+
+
+def _key(i: int) -> OffloadKey:
+    return make_offload_key(f"block-{i}".encode(), 0)
+
+
+def _file_mapper(root_dir: str) -> FileMapper:
+    return FileMapper(
+        root_dir=root_dir,
+        model_name="test",
+        tokens_per_hash=16,
+        blocks_per_file=1,
+        tp_size=1,
+        pp_size=1,
+        pcp_size=1,
+        dcp_size=1,
+        rank=0,
+        dtype="float16",
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def mapper(tmp_path) -> FileMapper:
+    return _file_mapper(str(tmp_path))
+
+
+@pytest.fixture
+def manager(mapper) -> Iterator[FSOffloadingManager]:
+    mgr = FSOffloadingManager(mapper, index_size=2)
+    yield mgr
+    mgr.shutdown()
+
+
+def _write_file(mapper: FileMapper, key: OffloadKey) -> None:
+    path = mapper.get_file_name(key)
+    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
+    with open(path, "wb") as f:
+        f.write(b"kv")
+
+
+def _store(manager: FSOffloadingManager, key: OffloadKey, success=True) -> None:
+    manager.prepare_store([key], _CTX, trigger=_TRIGGER)
+    manager.complete_store([key], _CTX, trigger=_TRIGGER, success=success)
+
+
+def _resolve(
+    manager: FSOffloadingManager, key: OffloadKey, timeout: float = 10.0
+) -> LookupResult:
+    """Drive scheduler steps until the async disk probe for key resolves."""
+    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
+    while (result := manager.lookup(key, _CTX)) is LookupResult.RETRY:
+        assert time.monotonic() < deadline, "disk lookup did not resolve"
+        manager.on_schedule_end(_STEP_END)
+        time.sleep(0.01)
+    return result
+
+
+def test_lookup_probes_disk(manager, mapper):
+    """Unknown keys are probed on disk asynchronously: RETRY until the probe
+    lands, then HIT for files another instance wrote, MISS otherwise."""
+    on_disk, absent = _key(1), _key(2)
+    _write_file(mapper, on_disk)
+
+    assert manager.lookup(on_disk, _CTX) is LookupResult.RETRY
+    assert _resolve(manager, on_disk) is LookupResult.HIT
+    assert _resolve(manager, absent) is LookupResult.MISS
+
+
+def test_disk_hit_is_remembered(manager, mapper):
+    """A key found on disk is indexed, so later lookups hit without probing,
+    even after its file is removed."""
+    key = _key(1)
+    _write_file(mapper, key)
+    assert _resolve(manager, key) is LookupResult.HIT
+
+    os.remove(mapper.get_file_name(key))
+    manager.on_request_finished(_CTX)
+    assert manager.lookup(key, _CTX) is LookupResult.HIT
+
+
+def test_in_flight_store_is_pending_and_not_restored(manager):
+    """A key whose store is in flight looks up as HIT_PENDING and is not
+    handed out to a second store job."""
+    key = _key(1)
+    first = manager.prepare_store([key], _CTX, trigger=_TRIGGER)
+    assert first is not None and first.keys_to_store == [key]
+
+    assert manager.lookup(key, _CTX) is LookupResult.HIT_PENDING
+    second = manager.prepare_store([key], _CTX, trigger=_TRIGGER)
+    assert second is not None and second.keys_to_store == []
+
+
+def test_successful_store_hits_and_is_not_restored(manager):
+    """A completed store is a HIT without a disk probe (no file exists here)
+    and is skipped by later stores."""
+    key = _key(1)
+    _store(manager, key)
+
+    assert manager.lookup(key, _CTX) is LookupResult.HIT
+    output = manager.prepare_store([key], _CTX, trigger=_TRIGGER)
+    assert output is not None and output.keys_to_store == []
+
+
+def test_failed_store_is_forgotten(manager):
+    """A failed store is neither pending nor indexed: lookups go back to disk
+    and the key can be stored again."""
+    key = _key(1)
+    _store(manager, key, success=False)
+
+    assert _resolve(manager, key) is LookupResult.MISS
+    output = manager.prepare_store([key], _CTX, trigger=_TRIGGER)
+    assert output is not None and output.keys_to_store == [key]
+
+
+def test_index_evicts_least_recently_used(manager):
+    """The index is a bounded LRU: a lookup refreshes a key, and the oldest
+    key is dropped once index_size is exceeded."""
+    k1, k2, k3 = _key(1), _key(2), _key(3)
+    _store(manager, k1)
+    _store(manager, k2)
+    assert manager.lookup(k1, _CTX) is LookupResult.HIT  # k2 is now oldest
+
+    _store(manager, k3)
+
+    assert manager.lookup(k1, _CTX) is LookupResult.HIT
+    assert manager.lookup(k3, _CTX) is LookupResult.HIT
+    assert _resolve(manager, k2) is LookupResult.MISS
+
+
+def test_reset_cache_drops_index_and_in_flight_stores(manager):
+    """After reset_cache, neither indexed nor in-flight keys are remembered,
+    so both can be stored again."""
+    stored, in_flight = _key(1), _key(2)
+    _store(manager, stored)
+    manager.prepare_store([in_flight], _CTX, trigger=_TRIGGER)
+
+    manager.reset_cache()
+
+    output = manager.prepare_store([stored, in_flight], _CTX, trigger=_TRIGGER)
+    assert output is not None
+    assert output.keys_to_store == [stored, in_flight]

+    readwrite, and exposes the flags the connector scheduler gates lookups
+    and store jobs on."""

+    of its own, so it still accepts a store if called directly."""

+    key = make_offload_key(b"block-hash", 0)
+
+    output = manager.prepare_store(
+        [key], ReqContext(req_id="r1"), trigger=StoreTrigger.ON_COMPUTE
+    )
+
+    assert output is not None
+    assert output.keys_to_store == [key]

+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Tests for GDSOffloadingWorker with cuFile replaced by a POSIX-backed fake.
+
+The fake turns each cuFile call into plain file I/O on the registered fd and
+records it, so the tests cover the worker's own logic (direct-path probe,
+temp-file publishing, cleanup) without GDS hardware.
+"""
+
+import os
+from collections.abc import Iterator
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.v1.kv_offload.base import (
+    CanonicalKVCaches,
+    CanonicalKVCacheTensor,
+)
+from vllm.v1.kv_offload.file_mapper import FileMapper
+from vllm.v1.kv_offload.fs.gds import worker as gds_worker
+from vllm.v1.kv_offload.fs.gds.cufile_bindings import CUfileBoolConfigParameter
+from vllm.v1.kv_offload.fs.gds.worker import GDSOffloadingWorker
+from vllm.v1.kv_offload.fs.worker import FileOp
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not current_platform.is_cuda(), reason="GDS offloading requires CUDA"
+)
+
+_PAGE_SIZE = 4096
+_HINT = "Run `gdscheck -p`"
+
+
+class FakeCuFile:
+    """POSIX stand-in for the cuFile bindings the worker uses.
+
+    A "device pointer" is written to the file as `_PAGE_SIZE`-byte chunks
+    of its low byte, so tests can tell which op landed where.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self.calls: list[tuple] = []
+        self.fail: str | None = None
+        self.short: str | None = None
+
+    def install(self, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
+        for name in (
+            "cuFileSetParameterBool",
+            "cuFileDriverOpen",
+            "cuFileDriverClose",
+            "cuFileHandleRegister",
+            "cuFileHandleDeregister",
+            "cuFileWrite",
+            "cuFileRead",
+        ):
+            monkeypatch.setattr(gds_worker, name, getattr(self, name))
+        # The real open_for_gds adds O_DIRECT, which tmpfs rejects.
+        monkeypatch.setattr(
+            gds_worker, "open_for_gds", lambda path, flags: os.open(path, flags, 0o644)
+        )
+
+    def _maybe_fail(self, name: str) -> None:
+        if self.fail == name:
+            raise RuntimeError(f"{name} failed: err=5008 (CU_FILE_IO_NOT_SUPPORTED)")
+
+    def op_names(self) -> list[str]:
+        return [c[0] for c in self.calls]
+
+    def cuFileSetParameterBool(self, param, value) -> None:
+        self._maybe_fail("cuFileSetParameterBool")
+        self.calls.append(("cuFileSetParameterBool", param, value))
+
+    def cuFileDriverOpen(self) -> None:
+        self._maybe_fail("cuFileDriverOpen")
+        self.calls.append(("cuFileDriverOpen",))
+
+    def cuFileDriverClose(self) -> None:
+        self.calls.append(("cuFileDriverClose",))
+
+    def cuFileHandleRegister(self, fd: int) -> int:
+        return fd
+
+    def cuFileHandleDeregister(self, handle: int) -> None:
+        pass
+
+    def cuFileWrite(self, fd: int, dev_ptr: int, size: int, file_offset: int) -> int:
+        self._maybe_fail("cuFileWrite")
+        self.calls.append(("cuFileWrite", dev_ptr, size, file_offset))
+        written = os.pwrite(fd, bytes([dev_ptr & 0xFF]) * size, file_offset)
+        return written - 1 if self.short == "cuFileWrite" else written
+
+    def cuFileRead(self, fd: int, dev_ptr: int, size: int, file_offset: int) -> int:
+        self._maybe_fail("cuFileRead")
+        self.calls.append(("cuFileRead", dev_ptr, size, file_offset))
+        read = len(os.pread(fd, size, file_offset))
+        return read - 1 if self.short == "cuFileRead" else read
+

+import importlib
+from collections.abc import Callable, Mapping

+

+
+class FSWorkerFactory:
+    """Registry for FSOffloadingWorker backends, resolved by fs_backend.
+
+    Mirrors OffloadingSpecFactory (vllm/v1/kv_offload/factory.py): built-in
+    backends are pre-registered below. External backends can either
+    register_backend() a friendly short name up front, or skip registration
+    and set fs_backend_module_path in the config -- see get_worker_cls.
+
+    Every backend is constructed as
+    cls(file_mapper=, blocks_per_file=, device=, kv_caches=, root_dir=,
+    extra_config=).
+    """
+
+    _registry: dict[str, Callable[[], type[FSOffloadingWorker]]] = {}
+
+    @classmethod
+    def register_backend(cls, name: str, module_path: str, class_name: str) -> None:
+        """Register a backend with a lazy-loading module and class name."""
+        if name in cls._registry:
+            raise ValueError(f"FS backend '{name}' is already registered.")
+
+        def loader() -> type[FSOffloadingWorker]:
+            module = importlib.import_module(module_path)
+            return getattr(module, class_name)
+
+        cls._registry[name] = loader
+
+    @classmethod
+    def get_worker_cls(
+        cls, extra_config: Mapping[str, Any]
+    ) -> type[FSOffloadingWorker]:
+        """Get the worker class named by extra_config["fs_backend"].
+
+        Args:
+            extra_config: kv_connector_extra_config. fs_backend (default
+                "gds") is checked against the registry first; if it is not
+                registered and fs_backend_module_path is set, fs_backend is
+                imported from there instead.
+
+        Returns:
+            The FSOffloadingWorker subclass.
+
+        Raises:
+            ValueError: If fs_backend is neither registered nor resolvable via
+                fs_backend_module_path.
+
+        """
+        name = extra_config.get("fs_backend", "gds")
+        if name in cls._registry:
+            worker_cls = cls._registry[name]()
+        else:
+            module_path = extra_config.get("fs_backend_module_path")
+            if module_path is None:
+                raise ValueError(
+                    f"Unknown fs_backend: {name!r}. Supported: {list(cls._registry)}. "
+                    "For an out-of-tree backend, also set fs_backend_module_path."
+                )
+            logger.warning_once(
+                "Loading out-of-tree FS offloading backend. This API is "
+                "experimental and subject to change in the future "
+                "as we iterate the design."
+            )
+            logger.info(
+                "Loading out-of-tree FS offloading backend '%s' from '%s'.",
+                name,
+                module_path,
+            )
+            module = importlib.import_module(module_path)
+            worker_cls = getattr(module, name)
+        assert issubclass(worker_cls, FSOffloadingWorker)
+        return worker_cls
+
+    @classmethod
+    def create_worker(
+        cls,
+        extra_config: Mapping[str, Any],
+        file_mapper: FileMapper,
+        blocks_per_file: int,
+        device: torch.device,
+        kv_caches: CanonicalKVCaches,
+        root_dir: str,
+    ) -> FSOffloadingWorker:
+        worker_cls = cls.get_worker_cls(extra_config)
+        logger.info("Creating FS offloading worker: %s", worker_cls.__name__)
+        return worker_cls(  # type: ignore[call-arg]
+            file_mapper=file_mapper,
+            blocks_per_file=blocks_per_file,
+            device=device,
+            kv_caches=kv_caches,
+            root_dir=root_dir,
+            extra_config=extra_config,
+        )
+
+
+FSWorkerFactory.register_backend(
+    "gds", "vllm.v1.kv_offload.fs.gds.worker", "GDSOffloadingWorker"
+)

+

+CU_FILE_SUCCESS = 0
+# cufile.h numbers its errors CUFILEOP_BASE_ERR + n; 0 is success.
+_CUFILEOP_BASE_ERR = 5000
+
+
+class CUfileOpError(IntEnum):
+    CU_FILE_SUCCESS = 0
+    CU_FILE_DRIVER_NOT_INITIALIZED = _CUFILEOP_BASE_ERR + 1
+    CU_FILE_DRIVER_INVALID_PROPS = _CUFILEOP_BASE_ERR + 2

+    CU_FILE_DRIVER_VERSION_READ_ERROR = _CUFILEOP_BASE_ERR + 5
+    CU_FILE_DRIVER_CLOSING = _CUFILEOP_BASE_ERR + 6
+    CU_FILE_PLATFORM_NOT_SUPPORTED = _CUFILEOP_BASE_ERR + 7
+    CU_FILE_IO_NOT_SUPPORTED = _CUFILEOP_BASE_ERR + 8
+    CU_FILE_DEVICE_NOT_SUPPORTED = _CUFILEOP_BASE_ERR + 9
+    CU_FILE_NVFS_DRIVER_ERROR = _CUFILEOP_BASE_ERR + 10
+    CU_FILE_CUDA_DRIVER_ERROR = _CUFILEOP_BASE_ERR + 11
+    CU_FILE_CUDA_POINTER_INVALID = _CUFILEOP_BASE_ERR + 12
+    CU_FILE_CUDA_MEMORY_TYPE_INVALID = _CUFILEOP_BASE_ERR + 13
+    CU_FILE_CUDA_POINTER_RANGE_ERROR = _CUFILEOP_BASE_ERR + 14
+    CU_FILE_CUDA_CONTEXT_MISMATCH = _CUFILEOP_BASE_ERR + 15
+    CU_FILE_INVALID_MAPPING_SIZE = _CUFILEOP_BASE_ERR + 16
+    CU_FILE_INVALID_MAPPING_RANGE = _CUFILEOP_BASE_ERR + 17
+    CU_FILE_INVALID_FILE_TYPE = _CUFILEOP_BASE_ERR + 18
+    CU_FILE_INVALID_FILE_OPEN_FLAG = _CUFILEOP_BASE_ERR + 19
+    CU_FILE_DIO_NOT_SET = _CUFILEOP_BASE_ERR + 20
+    CU_FILE_INVALID_VALUE = _CUFILEOP_BASE_ERR + 22
+    CU_FILE_MEMORY_ALREADY_REGISTERED = _CUFILEOP_BASE_ERR + 23
+    CU_FILE_MEMORY_NOT_REGISTERED = _CUFILEOP_BASE_ERR + 24
+    CU_FILE_PERMISSION_DENIED = _CUFILEOP_BASE_ERR + 25
+    CU_FILE_DRIVER_ALREADY_OPEN = _CUFILEOP_BASE_ERR + 26
+    CU_FILE_HANDLE_NOT_REGISTERED = _CUFILEOP_BASE_ERR + 27
+    CU_FILE_HANDLE_ALREADY_REGISTERED = _CUFILEOP_BASE_ERR + 28
+    CU_FILE_DEVICE_NOT_FOUND = _CUFILEOP_BASE_ERR + 29
+    CU_FILE_INTERNAL_ERROR = _CUFILEOP_BASE_ERR + 30
+    CU_FILE_GETNEWFD_FAILED = _CUFILEOP_BASE_ERR + 31
+    CU_FILE_NVFS_SETUP_ERROR = _CUFILEOP_BASE_ERR + 33
+    CU_FILE_IO_DISABLED = _CUFILEOP_BASE_ERR + 34
+    CU_FILE_BATCH_SUBMIT_FAILED = _CUFILEOP_BASE_ERR + 35
+    CU_FILE_GPU_MEMORY_PINNING_FAILED = _CUFILEOP_BASE_ERR + 36
+    CU_FILE_BATCH_FULL = _CUFILEOP_BASE_ERR + 37
+    CU_FILE_ASYNC_NOT_SUPPORTED = _CUFILEOP_BASE_ERR + 38
+    CU_FILE_IO_MAX_ERROR = _CUFILEOP_BASE_ERR + 39
+
+
+class CUfileBoolConfigParameter(IntEnum):
+    """CUFileBoolConfigParameter_t from cufile.h.
+
+    libcufile reads the numeric value, so these must track the C enum.
+    Values only ever get appended, which is why allow_compat_mode is
+    stable across cuFile releases.
+    """
+
+    CUFILE_PARAM_PROPERTIES_USE_POLL_MODE = 0
+    CUFILE_PARAM_PROPERTIES_ALLOW_COMPAT_MODE = 1
+    CUFILE_PARAM_FORCE_COMPAT_MODE = 2
+    CUFILE_PARAM_FS_MISC_API_CHECK_AGGRESSIVE = 3
+    CUFILE_PARAM_EXECUTION_PARALLEL_IO = 4
+    CUFILE_PARAM_PROFILE_NVTX = 5
+    CUFILE_PARAM_PROPERTIES_ALLOW_SYSTEM_MEMORY = 6
+    CUFILE_PARAM_USE_PCIP2PDMA = 7
+    CUFILE_PARAM_PREFER_IO_URING = 8
+    CUFILE_PARAM_FORCE_ODIRECT_MODE = 9
+    CUFILE_PARAM_SKIP_TOPOLOGY_DETECTION = 10
+    CUFILE_PARAM_STREAM_MEMOPS_BYPASS = 11
+
+
+class CUfileError_t(Structure):
+    _fields_ = [
+        ("err", c_int),  # CUfileOpError
+        ("cu_err", c_int),  # CUDA driver error
+    ]
+
+
+class _HandleUnion(Union):
+    _fields_ = [
+        ("fd", c_int),  # Linux POSIX fd
+        ("handle", c_void_p),  # Windows handle
+    ]
+
+
+class CUfileDescr_t(Structure):
+    _fields_ = [
+        ("type", c_uint),  # CUfileFileHandleType
+        ("handle", _HandleUnion),
+        ("fs_ops", c_void_p),  # const CUfileFSOps_t*
+    ]
+
+
+CUfileHandle_t = c_void_p
+
+_lib: ctypes.CDLL | None = None
+
+
+def _get_lib() -> ctypes.CDLL:
+    global _lib
+    if _lib is not None:
+        return _lib
+
+    # use_errno so sync-API failures can report the real errno.
+    lib_path = ctypes.util.find_library("cufile")
+    if lib_path is None:
+        for candidate in ("libcufile.so.0", "libcufile.so"):
+            try:
+                _lib = ctypes.CDLL(candidate, mode=ctypes.RTLD_GLOBAL, use_errno=True)
+                return _lib
+            except OSError:
+                continue
+        raise OSError(
+            "Cannot find libcufile.so. Ensure nvidia-cufile is installed "
+            "and the library is on LD_LIBRARY_PATH."
+        )
+    _lib = ctypes.CDLL(lib_path, mode=ctypes.RTLD_GLOBAL, use_errno=True)
+    return _lib
+
+
+def _get_function(lib: ctypes.CDLL, name: str, min_version: str):
+    try:
+        return getattr(lib, name)
+    except AttributeError as e:
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            f"libcufile does not export {name}; nvidia-cufile >= "
+            f"{min_version} is required."
+        ) from e
+
+
+def _check_error(err: CUfileError_t, func_name: str) -> None:
+    if err.err != CU_FILE_SUCCESS:
+        try:
+            err_name = CUfileOpError(err.err).name
+        except ValueError:
+            err_name = f"UNKNOWN({err.err})"
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            f"{func_name} failed: err={err.err} ({err_name}), cu_err={err.cu_err}"
+        )
+
+
+def cuFileSetParameterBool(param: CUfileBoolConfigParameter, value: bool) -> None:
+    """Stage a boolean cuFile parameter.
+

+    driver load, and the call fails with CU_FILE_DRIVER_ALREADY_OPEN once
+    the driver is open.
+    """
+    lib = _get_lib()
+    fn = _get_function(lib, "cuFileSetParameterBool", "1.14")
+    fn.restype = CUfileError_t
+    fn.argtypes = [c_int, c_bool]
+    err = fn(int(param), c_bool(value))
+    _check_error(err, f"cuFileSetParameterBool({param.name})")
+
+
+def cuFileDriverOpen() -> None:
+    lib = _get_lib()
+    lib.cuFileDriverOpen.restype = CUfileError_t
+    lib.cuFileDriverOpen.argtypes = []
+    err = lib.cuFileDriverOpen()
+    _check_error(err, "cuFileDriverOpen")
+
+
+def cuFileDriverClose() -> None:
+    lib = _get_lib()
+    lib.cuFileDriverClose.restype = CUfileError_t
+    lib.cuFileDriverClose.argtypes = []
+    err = lib.cuFileDriverClose()
+    _check_error(err, "cuFileDriverClose")
+
+
+def cuFileBufRegister(dev_ptr: int, size: int, flags: int = 0) -> None:
+    """Register a device memory range for cuFile I/O."""
+    lib = _get_lib()
+    lib.cuFileBufRegister.restype = CUfileError_t
+    lib.cuFileBufRegister.argtypes = [c_void_p, c_size_t, c_int]
+    err = lib.cuFileBufRegister(c_void_p(dev_ptr), c_size_t(size), c_int(flags))
+    _check_error(err, "cuFileBufRegister")
+
+
+def cuFileBufDeregister(dev_ptr: int) -> None:
+    lib = _get_lib()
+    lib.cuFileBufDeregister.restype = CUfileError_t
+    lib.cuFileBufDeregister.argtypes = [c_void_p]
+    err = lib.cuFileBufDeregister(c_void_p(dev_ptr))
+    _check_error(err, "cuFileBufDeregister")
+
+
+def cuFileHandleRegister(fd: int) -> CUfileHandle_t:
+    """Register a POSIX file descriptor for cuFile I/O."""
+    lib = _get_lib()
+    lib.cuFileHandleRegister.restype = CUfileError_t
+    lib.cuFileHandleRegister.argtypes = [
+        POINTER(CUfileHandle_t),
+        POINTER(CUfileDescr_t),
+    ]
+
+    descr = CUfileDescr_t()
+    descr.type = CU_FILE_HANDLE_TYPE_OPAQUE_FD
+    descr.handle.fd = fd
+    descr.fs_ops = None
+
+    handle = CUfileHandle_t()
+    err = lib.cuFileHandleRegister(ctypes.byref(handle), ctypes.byref(descr))
+    _check_error(err, "cuFileHandleRegister")
+    return handle
+
+
+def cuFileHandleDeregister(handle: CUfileHandle_t) -> None:
+    lib = _get_lib()
+    lib.cuFileHandleDeregister.restype = None
+    lib.cuFileHandleDeregister.argtypes = [CUfileHandle_t]
+    lib.cuFileHandleDeregister(handle)
+
+
+def _io_error(op: str, ret: int) -> RuntimeError:
+    # Sync I/O returns -1 with errno set for OS errors, or the negated
+    # CUfileOpError for cuFile errors.
+    if ret != -1:
+        try:
+            return RuntimeError(f"{op} failed: ret={ret} ({CUfileOpError(-ret).name})")
+        except ValueError:
+            pass
+    err = ctypes.get_errno()
+    return RuntimeError(f"{op} failed: ret={ret}, errno={err} ({os.strerror(err)})")
+
+
+def cuFileRead(
+    handle: CUfileHandle_t,
+    dev_ptr: int,
+    size: int,
+    file_offset: int = 0,
+    buf_offset: int = 0,
+) -> int:
+    """Synchronous read from file to GPU memory. Returns bytes read."""
+    lib = _get_lib()
+    lib.cuFileRead.restype = c_ssize_t
+    lib.cuFileRead.argtypes = [
+        CUfileHandle_t,
+        c_void_p,
+        c_size_t,
+        c_ssize_t,
+        c_ssize_t,
+    ]
+    ctypes.set_errno(0)
+    ret = lib.cuFileRead(
+        handle,
+        c_void_p(dev_ptr),
+        c_size_t(size),
+        c_ssize_t(file_offset),
+        c_ssize_t(buf_offset),
+    )
+    if ret < 0:
+        raise _io_error("cuFileRead", ret)
+    return ret
+
+
+def cuFileWrite(
+    handle: CUfileHandle_t,
+    dev_ptr: int,
+    size: int,
+    file_offset: int = 0,
+    buf_offset: int = 0,
+) -> int:
+    """Synchronous write from GPU memory to file. Returns bytes written."""
+    lib = _get_lib()
+    lib.cuFileWrite.restype = c_ssize_t
+    lib.cuFileWrite.argtypes = [
+        CUfileHandle_t,
+        c_void_p,
+        c_size_t,
+        c_ssize_t,
+        c_ssize_t,
+    ]
+    ctypes.set_errno(0)
+    ret = lib.cuFileWrite(
+        handle,
+        c_void_p(dev_ptr),
+        c_size_t(size),
+        c_ssize_t(file_offset),
+        c_ssize_t(buf_offset),
+    )
+    if ret < 0:
+        raise _io_error("cuFileWrite", ret)
+    return ret
+
+
+def open_for_gds(path: str, flags: int) -> int:
+    """Open a file with O_DIRECT for GDS I/O. Returns the fd."""
+    O_DIRECT = getattr(os, "O_DIRECT", 0)
+    return os.open(path, flags | O_DIRECT, 0o644)

+"""GDS offloading worker — direct GPU<->NVMe via cuFile sync API."""
+
+import contextlib
+import os
+import uuid
+from typing import Any
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.v1.kv_offload.base import CanonicalKVCaches
+from vllm.v1.kv_offload.file_mapper import FileMapper
+from vllm.v1.kv_offload.fs.gds.cufile_bindings import (
+    CUfileBoolConfigParameter,
+    cuFileDriverClose,
+    cuFileDriverOpen,
+    cuFileHandleDeregister,
+    cuFileHandleRegister,
+    cuFileRead,
+    cuFileSetParameterBool,
+    cuFileWrite,
+    open_for_gds,
+)
+from vllm.v1.kv_offload.fs.worker import FileOp, ThreadPoolFSWorker
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+
+class GDSOffloadingWorker(ThreadPoolFSWorker):
+    """GPU<->NVMe transfers via NVIDIA cuFile synchronous API.
+
+    Each file's I/O is submitted to a thread pool so multiple operations
+    overlap on the NVMe device (higher queue depth = higher throughput).
+
+    All file syscalls (open, cuFileHandleRegister, I/O,
+    cuFileHandleDeregister, close) run inside pool threads to keep the
+    scheduler thread free of blocking operations.  Driver open/close and
+    the direct-path probe (_validate_gds) run on the caller's
+    thread at init/shutdown.
+
+    Compat mode is disabled, so cuFile cannot silently fall back to POSIX
+    I/O through bounce buffers.  At init the worker round-trips one KV
+    block through root_dir to prove the direct path works on that mount.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        file_mapper: FileMapper,
+        blocks_per_file: int,
+        device: torch.device,
+        kv_caches: CanonicalKVCaches,
+        root_dir: str,
+        extra_config: dict[str, Any],
+    ):
+        if not current_platform.is_cuda():
+            raise RuntimeError("GDS offloading requires an NVIDIA CUDA GPU.")
+        io_threads = int(extra_config.get("gds_max_io_threads", 32))
+        super().__init__(
+            file_mapper=file_mapper,
+            blocks_per_file=blocks_per_file,
+            device=device,
+            max_io_threads=io_threads,
+        )
+        self._driver_open = False
+        try:
+            self._validate_gds(device, kv_caches, root_dir, io_threads)
+        except Exception:
+            self.shutdown_dispatch()
+            self.shutdown_backend()
+            raise
+
+    def _validate_gds(
+        self,
+        device: torch.device,
+        kv_caches: CanonicalKVCaches,
+        root_dir: str,
+        io_threads: int,
+    ) -> None:
+        """Open cuFile with compat mode off and prove the direct path works.
+
+        Takes one KV block (block 0 of the first KV tensor), writes it to
+        a temp file under root_dir, reads it back, and deletes the file.  With
+        compat mode off cuFile has no POSIX fallback, so success means
+        GPU<->storage DMA works on this mount.  The data is not checked, only
+        that both transfers complete.  This runs before the KV cache holds
+        any data, so the read may overwrite the block freely.
+        """
+        # Staged parameters only apply at driver load, so this must come
+        # before cuFileDriverOpen.
+        cuFileSetParameterBool(
+            CUfileBoolConfigParameter.CUFILE_PARAM_PROPERTIES_ALLOW_COMPAT_MODE,
+            False,
+        )
+        cuFileDriverOpen()
+        self._driver_open = True
+
+        # A uint8 view of block 0 of the first KV tensor.
+        kv = kv_caches.tensors[0]
+        size = kv.page_size_bytes
+        storage = kv.tensor.untyped_storage()
+        block = torch.empty(0, dtype=torch.uint8, device=device)
+        block.set_(storage, kv.tensor.data_ptr() - storage.data_ptr(), (size,))
+        ptr = block.data_ptr()
+
+        os.makedirs(root_dir, exist_ok=True)
+        path = os.path.join(root_dir, f".gds_probe_{uuid.uuid4().hex}.tmp")
+        with torch.accelerator.device_index(device.index):
+            try:
+                fd = open_for_gds(path, os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_WRONLY)
+                try:
+                    handle = cuFileHandleRegister(fd)
+                    try:
+                        ret = cuFileWrite(handle, ptr, size, 0)
+                    finally:
+                        cuFileHandleDeregister(handle)
+                finally:
+                    os.close(fd)
+                if ret != size:
+                    raise RuntimeError(f"cuFileWrite short write: {ret}/{size}")
+
+                fd = open_for_gds(path, os.O_RDONLY)
+                try:
+                    handle = cuFileHandleRegister(fd)
+                    try:
+                        ret = cuFileRead(handle, ptr, size, 0)
+                    finally:
+                        cuFileHandleDeregister(handle)
+                finally:
+                    os.close(fd)
+                if ret != size:
+                    raise RuntimeError(f"cuFileRead short read: {ret}/{size}")
+            except Exception as e:
+                raise RuntimeError(
+                    f"GDS direct-path probe failed under root_dir={root_dir!r} "
+                    f"with compat mode disabled: {e}. Run `gdscheck -p` to check "
+                    "that GDS is supported for this filesystem and GPU."
+                ) from e
+            finally:
+                with contextlib.suppress(FileNotFoundError):
+                    os.remove(path)
+        logger.info("GDS: direct path verified (compat disabled)")
+
+    def write_block(self, file_path: str, ops: list[FileOp]) -> None:
+        """Write to a temp file, then atomically rename it into place, so
+        readers never see a partially written file."""
+        # File names are content hashes: an existing file holds this block.
+        if os.path.exists(file_path):
+            return
+        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(file_path), exist_ok=True)
+        tmp_path = f"{file_path}_{uuid.uuid4().hex}.tmp"
+        try:
+            fd = open_for_gds(tmp_path, os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_WRONLY)
+            try:
+                handle = cuFileHandleRegister(fd)
+                try:
+                    for op in ops:
+                        ret = cuFileWrite(
+                            handle, op.device_ptr, op.size_bytes, op.file_offset
+                        )
+                        if ret != op.size_bytes:
+                            raise RuntimeError(
+                                f"cuFileWrite short write: {ret}/{op.size_bytes}"
+                            )
+                finally:
+                    cuFileHandleDeregister(handle)
+            finally:
+                os.close(fd)
+            try:
+                os.replace(tmp_path, file_path)
+            except FileExistsError:
+                # Some shared filesystems fail the rename with EEXIST instead
+                # of replacing; another writer already published this block.
+                with contextlib.suppress(OSError):
+                    os.remove(tmp_path)
+        except Exception:
+            try:
+                os.remove(tmp_path)
+            except FileNotFoundError:
+                pass
+            except OSError as cleanup_exc:
+                logger.warning(
+                    "Failed to remove temp file %s: %s", tmp_path, cleanup_exc
+                )
+            raise
+
+    def read_block(self, file_path: str, ops: list[FileOp]) -> None:
+        fd = open_for_gds(file_path, os.O_RDONLY)
+        try:
+            handle = cuFileHandleRegister(fd)
+            try:
+                for op in ops:
+                    ret = cuFileRead(
+                        handle, op.device_ptr, op.size_bytes, op.file_offset
+                    )
+                    if ret != op.size_bytes:
+                        raise RuntimeError(
+                            f"cuFileRead short read: {ret}/{op.size_bytes}"
+                        )
+            finally:
+                cuFileHandleDeregister(handle)
+        finally:
+            os.close(fd)
+
+    def shutdown_backend(self) -> None:
+        if self._driver_open:
+            self._driver_open = False
+            try:
+                cuFileDriverClose()
+            except RuntimeError as e:
+                logger.warning("cuFileDriverClose failed: %s", e)
+        logger.info("GDS worker shut down")

+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Scheduler-side manager for direct device <-> filesystem offloading."""
+
+from collections import OrderedDict
+from collections.abc import Collection
+
+from typing_extensions import override
+
+from vllm.v1.kv_offload.base import (
+    LoadStoreSpec,
+    LookupResult,
+    Medium,
+    OffloadingManager,
+    OffloadKey,
+    PrepareStoreOutput,
+    ReqContext,
+    RequestOffloadingContext,
+    ScheduleEndContext,
+    StoreTrigger,
+)
+from vllm.v1.kv_offload.file_mapper import FileMapper
+from vllm.v1.kv_offload.fs.common import FSLoadStoreSpec
+from vllm.v1.kv_offload.fs.lookup import FsAsyncLookupManager
+from vllm.v1.metrics.cache_hit_source import CacheHitSource
+
+DEFAULT_INDEX_SIZE = 100_000
+
+
+class FSOffloadingManager(OffloadingManager):
+    """Tracks content-addressed KV files that the worker moves to and from
+    device memory directly, unlike FileSystemTierManager, which stages
+    through the CPU tier.
+
+    Keys are looked up on disk asynchronously, so files written by other
+    instances or earlier runs are reused. Keys found on disk or stored by
+    this instance are remembered in a bounded LRU index, so later requests
+    hit without probing again. Dropping a key from the index leaves its
+    file on disk.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        file_mapper: FileMapper,
+        index_size: int = DEFAULT_INDEX_SIZE,
+    ):
+        assert index_size > 0
+        self.medium = Medium.STORAGE
+        self._index_size = index_size
+        self._index: OrderedDict[OffloadKey, None] = OrderedDict()
+        # Keys whose store is in flight; their files may be incomplete.
+        self._storing: set[OffloadKey] = set()
+        self._fs_lookup = FsAsyncLookupManager(file_mapper, tier_type="fs")
+
+    def _remember(self, key: OffloadKey) -> None:
+        self._index[key] = None
+        self._index.move_to_end(key)
+        if len(self._index) > self._index_size:
+            self._index.popitem(last=False)
+
+    @override
+    def on_new_request(self, req_context: ReqContext) -> RequestOffloadingContext:
+        return RequestOffloadingContext()
+
+    @override
+    def lookup(self, key: OffloadKey, req_context: ReqContext) -> LookupResult:
+        if key in self._index:
+            self._index.move_to_end(key)
+            return LookupResult.HIT
+        if key in self._storing:
+            return LookupResult.HIT_PENDING
+        found = self._fs_lookup.lookup(key, req_context)
+        if found is None:
+            return LookupResult.RETRY
+        if not found:
+            return LookupResult.MISS
+        self._remember(key)
+        return LookupResult.HIT
+
+    @override
+    def get_load_source(
+        self, key: OffloadKey, req_context: ReqContext
+    ) -> CacheHitSource:
+        return CacheHitSource.DISK
+
+    @override
+    def prepare_load(
+        self, keys: Collection[OffloadKey], req_context: ReqContext
+    ) -> LoadStoreSpec:
+        return FSLoadStoreSpec(list(keys))
+
+    @override
+    def prepare_store(
+        self,
+        keys: Collection[OffloadKey],
+        req_context: ReqContext,
+        *,
+        trigger: StoreTrigger,
+    ) -> PrepareStoreOutput | None:
+        keys_to_store = [
+            k for k in keys if k not in self._index and k not in self._storing
+        ]
+        self._storing.update(keys_to_store)
+        # Empty, not None: None counts as an allocation failure.
+        return PrepareStoreOutput(
+            keys_to_store=keys_to_store,
+            store_spec=FSLoadStoreSpec(keys_to_store),
+            evicted_keys=[],
+        )
+
+    @override
+    def complete_store(
+        self,
+        keys: Collection[OffloadKey],
+        req_context: ReqContext,
+        *,
+        trigger: StoreTrigger,
+        success: bool = True,
+    ) -> None:
+        for key in keys:
+            self._storing.discard(key)
+            if success:
+                self._remember(key)
+        if success:
+            self._fs_lookup.mark_present(keys)
+
+    @override
+    def on_schedule_end(self, context: ScheduleEndContext) -> None:
+        self._fs_lookup.flush()
+
+    @override
+    def on_request_finished(self, req_context: ReqContext) -> None:
+        self._fs_lookup.cleanup(req_context.req_id)
+
+    @override
+    def reset_cache(self) -> None:
+        # Pre-reset jobs never reach complete_store, so drop them here too.
+        self._index.clear()
+        self._storing.clear()
+
+    @override
+    def shutdown(self) -> None:
+        self._fs_lookup.shutdown()

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

+"""Spec for direct device <-> filesystem offloading."""
+
+from typing_extensions import override

+from vllm.v1.kv_offload.base import (

+from vllm.v1.kv_offload.fs.manager import DEFAULT_INDEX_SIZE, FSOffloadingManager
+
+
+class FSOffloadingSpec(OffloadingSpec):
+    """Offloads KV directly between device memory and files, with the worker
+    backend picked by the fs_backend key (see FSWorkerFactory)."""
+
+    def __init__(self, config: OffloadingConfig):
+        super().__init__(config)
+        # Fail at startup, on the scheduler too, if the backend is unknown.
+        FSWorkerFactory.get_worker_cls(self.extra_config)
+        root_dir = self.extra_config.get("root_dir")
+        if not root_dir:
+            raise ValueError("root_dir must be specified in kv_connector_extra_config")
+        self.root_dir: str = root_dir
+        self.index_size = int(
+            self.extra_config.get("fs_index_size", DEFAULT_INDEX_SIZE)
+        )
+        # Same naming as the FS secondary tier, so either can read the other's
+        # files.
+        self.file_mapper = FileMapper.from_offloading_spec(
+            root_dir=root_dir,
+            offloading_spec=self,
+            blocks_per_file=self.blocks_per_chunk,
+            parallel_agnostic=True,
+        )
+
+        self._manager: OffloadingManager | None = None
+        self._worker: OffloadingWorker | None = None
+
+    @override
+    def get_manager(self) -> OffloadingManager:
+        if self._manager is None:
+            self._manager = FSOffloadingManager(
+                file_mapper=self.file_mapper,
+                index_size=self.index_size,
+            )
+        return self._manager
+
+    @override
+    def get_worker(self, kv_caches: CanonicalKVCaches) -> OffloadingWorker:
+        if self._worker is None:
+            self._worker = FSWorkerFactory.create_worker(
+                self.extra_config,
+                file_mapper=self.file_mapper,
+                blocks_per_file=self.blocks_per_chunk,
+                device=kv_caches.tensors[0].tensor.device,
+                kv_caches=kv_caches,
+                root_dir=self.root_dir,
+            )
+        return self._worker

Signed-off-by: Ansat <47277869+sansblues@users.noreply.github.com>

@@ -6773,6 +6773,65 @@ def test_mamba_sparse_retention_caches_decode_resume_state_on_free(lookahead):
     assert [len(blocks) for blocks in computed_blocks.blocks] == [6, 6]
 
 
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("async_scheduling", [False, True])
+def test_mamba_decode_resume_skips_off_boundary_checkpoint_block(async_scheduling):
+    """A resumed prefill over [0, 95) runs in one pass and exports its checkpoint
+    at 80 into the Mamba block ending at 64. That block must not be cached on
+    free as the decode state at 64, also after later steps were scheduled."""
+    hash_block_size, mamba_block_size = 16, 64
+    kv_cache_config = _make_hybrid_kv_cache_config(
+        hash_block_size, 100, ["full", "mamba"]
+    )
+    _replace_group(
+        kv_cache_config,
+        1,
+        block_size=mamba_block_size,
+        num_prefill_checkpoint_blocks=1,
+        prefill_checkpoint_alignment=hash_block_size,
+    )
+    manager = make_kv_cache_manager(
+        kv_cache_config,
+        max_model_len=8192,
+        enable_caching=True,
+        hash_block_size=hash_block_size,
+        retention_interval=0,
+    )
+    # A preempted request: 50 prompt tokens, then 45 output tokens to replay.
+    req = make_request("0", list(range(50)), hash_block_size, sha256)
+    for token in range(1000, 1045):
+        req.append_output_token_ids(token)
+
+    # Mirror the scheduler: a step is scheduled, then its output arrives.
+    def schedule(num_new_tokens: int) -> int:
+        manager.new_step_starts()
+        assert manager.allocate_slots(req, num_new_tokens) is not None
+        req.num_computed_tokens += num_new_tokens
+        req.num_in_flight_tokens += num_new_tokens
+        return num_new_tokens
+
+    def finish(num_scheduled_tokens: int) -> None:
+        req.num_in_flight_tokens -= num_scheduled_tokens
+        req.append_output_token_ids(7)
+
+    resumed_prefill = schedule(95)
+    if async_scheduling:
+        # The next step is scheduled before the resumed prefill finishes.
+        decode = schedule(1)
+        finish(resumed_prefill)
+        schedule(1)
+        finish(decode)
+    else:
+        finish(resumed_prefill)
+        schedule(1)
+    manager.free(req)
+

All KV cache groups share a single `FreeKVCacheBlockQueue` organized into three eviction tiers: uncached blocks at the front, a middle deprioritized tier (FIFO, inserted before `_cached_head`), and normal LRU-cached blocks at the tail. +Models with mamba layers + full attention layers support prefix caching via the full attention + X algorithm in case 2, with the Mamba state cached at block boundaries.
+
+Because recurrent checkpoints from older turns accumulate across every Mamba KV cache group, vLLM enables superseded-state deprioritization by default whenever prefix caching is active for Mamba groups. When a finished request caches a deeper Mamba tip past an earlier tip, the immediate predecessor (`t-1`) remains in normal LRU as a one-turn rollback fallback (and shared-prefix junctions or multi-branch fork points stay in normal LRU), while states two or more turns behind (`t-2` and older) are moved to the middle deprioritized tier. Deprioritized blocks keep their hashes until reused, so they are evicted after uncached blocks and before normal LRU-cached blocks (such as active full-attention KV blocks). See [Automatic Prefix Caching](../features/automatic_prefix_caching.md).

+### Superseded Mamba state eviction
+
+With prefix caching enabled, vLLM automatically deprioritizes superseded Mamba checkpoints in multi-turn workloads with no extra configuration:

+- **Eviction order**: `uncached -> deprioritized (FIFO) -> normal LRU cached`. Deprioritized blocks keep their prefix hashes while free blocks remain and are only evicted ahead of normal LRU-cached blocks under memory pressure.
+- **One-turn fallback protection**: when a finished request advances a conversation's cached Mamba tip, the immediate predecessor (`t-1`) stays in normal LRU to shield against small tail rollbacks (such as tool retries), while states two or more turns behind (`t-2` and older) are deprioritized.

+The DP/EP prepare paths quantize with row-major scales for the a2a and
+restore the swizzled 128x4 layout afterwards; the result must be
+bit-identical to quantizing directly into the swizzled layout, and scales
+for kernels that take row-major scales must pass through unchanged.

+    mxfp8_e4m3_quantize,

+if not current_platform.is_cuda():

+    )

+    torch.manual_seed(0)

+    _, want = mxfp8_e4m3_quantize(x, is_sf_swizzled_layout=True)

@@ -112,6 +113,12 @@ Both lists are capped at the same `max_budget`.
 
 **Post-processing.** The `postprocess_encoder_output` method receives an `outputs` dictionary keyed by path name. The model is responsible for assembling global and local features into the final per-image embedding. For DeepSeek-OCR, it reshapes the global output into `[B, 272, n_embed]`, reshapes the local output into `[P, 100, n_embed]`, assembles patch grids with newline tokens, and concatenating `[patches_grid, global, view_separator]` for each image.
 
+DeepSeek-OCR-2 uses the same two-path capture policy with 256 output tokens per
+global image and 144 per local tile. The local path is skipped for images that
+do not need tiling. Its post-processing concatenates the local tiles in image
+order, the global image features, and the view separator; unlike DeepSeek-OCR,
+it does not insert newline tokens.
+
 !!! note
     The dual-path design enables partial CUDA graph coverage — one path can hit while the other falls back to eager. This avoids wasted compute on zero-padded patch buffers for untiled images and avoids graph invalidation caused by variable `crop_shape` per image.
