@@ -0,0 +1,607 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Microbenchmark for the `_copy_mamba_state_block` device function.
+
+Isolates the per-(request, state, tile) mamba state copy body from the surrounding
+postprocess decision logic. The copy metadata comes from the production
+`MambaSpecDecodeGPUContext`, and every config checks the copy before timing
+it. `--model` takes any HF hybrid model with a conv +
+temporal state per layer; its layout (tp=1) comes from vLLM's own state
+shape/dtype logic. The presets listed by `--list-models` work offline.
+
+Grid mirrors the fused-kernel launch shape
+(num_reqs, total_states, temporal_tiles).
+
+Usage:
+    # nsys (whole-run trace)
+    nsys profile -t cuda,nvtx --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi \
+      --force-overwrite=true -o bench_copy_mamba \
+      python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_copy_mamba_state_block.py
+
+    nsys stats --report cuda_gpu_kern_sum bench_copy_mamba.nsys-rep \
+      | grep -i bench_copy_mamba_state_block
+
+    # ncu (kernel metrics; use --nvtx-include to slice per-config, and -k to
+    # skip the L2-flush kernels that also run inside each range).
+    # The trailing "/" is Nsight's push/pop match marker, not part of the name;
+    # the range names below intentionally contain no "/" so they parse.
+    ncu --set full --nvtx --nvtx-include "reqs=64_conv=SD_tiles=16/" \
+      -k regex:bench_copy_mamba_state_block -o bench_copy_mamba \
+      python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_copy_mamba_state_block.py
+
+    # CUPTI kernel timing only (cold L2, median per config; needs
+    # cupti-python >= 13, otherwise FlashInfer falls back to CUDA events):
+    python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_copy_mamba_state_block.py
+
+    # Any HF hybrid model (fetches its config):
+    python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_copy_mamba_state_block.py \
+      --model ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-tiny
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import math
+import os
+import statistics
+import time
+from dataclasses import dataclass, replace
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import torch
+import torch.cuda.nvtx as nvtx
+from flashinfer.testing import bench_gpu_time_with_cupti
+
+from vllm.engine.arg_utils import EngineArgs
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.mamba.mamba_utils import (
+    get_conv_copy_spec,
+    get_conv_state_layout,
+    get_temporal_copy_spec,
+    is_conv_state_dim_first,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.models import ModelRegistry
+from vllm.transformers_utils.config import get_config, get_hf_text_config
+from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton
+from vllm.v1.core.single_type_kv_cache_manager import MambaManager
+from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import KVCacheConfig, KVCacheGroup, MambaSpec
+from vllm.v1.worker.mamba_utils import (
+    _TEMPORAL_TILES,
+    MambaSpecDecodeGPUContext,
+    _copy_mamba_state_block,
+)
+
+DEVICE = "cuda"
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class ModelStateConfig:
+    """State layout parameters for one hybrid-mamba model at tp=1.
+
+    All values are derived from the model's HF config plus a chosen num_spec.
+    Conv/temporal shapes here are per-block (num_blocks is added at runtime).
+    """
+
+    name: str
+    num_state_layers: int
+    conv_dim: int
+    conv_state_len: int
+    temporal_shape: tuple[int, ...]
+    conv_dtype: torch.dtype
+    temporal_dtype: torch.dtype
+    num_spec: int
+    layer_kind: str  # "gated_delta_net", "mamba2", or the HF architecture
+    notes: str = ""
+
+    @property
+    def total_states(self) -> int:
+        return self.num_state_layers * 2  # conv + temporal
+
+
+# Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B: gated delta net, 24 linear + 8 full-attn out of 32.
+# See huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B/config.json and
+# MambaStateShapeCalculator.gated_delta_net_state_shape.
+#   conv_dim = head_k*num_k_heads*2 + head_v*num_v_heads
+#            = 128*16*2 + 128*32 = 8192
+#   temporal = (num_v_heads, head_v_dim, head_k_dim) = (32, 128, 128)
+_QWEN3_5_9B = ModelStateConfig(
+    name="Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B",
+    num_state_layers=24,
+    conv_dim=8192,
+    conv_state_len=4 - 1 + 2,  # conv_kernel - 1 + num_spec
+    temporal_shape=(32, 128, 128),
+    conv_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+    temporal_dtype=torch.float32,  # mamba_ssm_dtype in the HF config
+    num_spec=2,
+    layer_kind="gated_delta_net",
+    notes="24 linear + 8 full_attention (interval 4) out of 32",
+)
+
+# nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-NVFP4: mamba2, 40 M + 8 * + 40 E
+# out of 88 layers (hybrid_override_pattern in HF config).
+# See huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-NVFP4/config.json
+# and MambaStateShapeCalculator.mamba2_state_shape.
+#   intermediate = mamba_num_heads * mamba_head_dim = 128*64 = 8192
+#   conv_dim = intermediate + 2*n_groups*ssm_state_size
+#            = 8192 + 2*8*128 = 10240
+#   temporal = (mamba_num_heads, mamba_head_dim, ssm_state_size)
+#            = (128, 64, 128)
+# num_spec=1 matches num_nextn_predict_layers in the HF config.
+_NEMOTRON3_SUPER_120B = ModelStateConfig(
+    name="nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-NVFP4",
+    num_state_layers=40,
+    conv_dim=10240,
+    conv_state_len=4 - 1 + 1,  # conv_kernel - 1 + num_spec
+    temporal_shape=(128, 64, 128),
+    conv_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+    temporal_dtype=torch.float32,  # mamba_ssm_cache_dtype in the HF config
+    num_spec=1,
+    layer_kind="mamba2",
+    notes="40 mamba + 8 attention + 40 moe out of 88",
+)
+
+# Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B: gated delta net, 18 linear + 6 full-attn out of 24.
+# See huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B/config.json and
+# MambaStateShapeCalculator.gated_delta_net_state_shape.
+#   conv_dim = head_k*num_k_heads*2 + head_v*num_v_heads
+#            = 128*16*2 + 128*16 = 6144
+#   temporal = (num_v_heads, head_v_dim, head_k_dim) = (16, 128, 128)
+_QWEN3_5_0_8B = ModelStateConfig(
+    name="Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B",
+    num_state_layers=18,
+    conv_dim=6144,
+    conv_state_len=4 - 1 + 2,  # conv_kernel - 1 + num_spec
+    temporal_shape=(16, 128, 128),
+    conv_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+    temporal_dtype=torch.float32,  # mamba_ssm_dtype in the HF config
+    num_spec=2,
+    layer_kind="gated_delta_net",
+    notes="18 linear + 6 full_attention (interval 4) out of 24",
+)
+
+MODEL_CONFIGS: dict[str, ModelStateConfig] = {
+    _QWEN3_5_9B.name: _QWEN3_5_9B,
+    _QWEN3_5_0_8B.name: _QWEN3_5_0_8B,
+    _NEMOTRON3_SUPER_120B.name: _NEMOTRON3_SUPER_120B,
+}
+
+
+def model_state_config_from_hf(
+    model: str, num_spec: int | None, trust_remote_code: bool
+) -> ModelStateConfig:
+    """Derive the state layout of `model` from vLLM's own shape/dtype logic.
+
+    `num_spec=None` uses the model's MTP layer count from its HF config.
+    """
+    if num_spec is None:
+        hf_text_config = get_hf_text_config(get_config(model, trust_remote_code))
+        num_spec = (
+            getattr(hf_text_config, "mtp_num_hidden_layers", None)
+            or getattr(hf_text_config, "num_nextn_predict_layers", None)
+            or 0
+        )
+    # ngram loads no draft model; only num_speculative_tokens affects shapes.
+    speculative_config = (
+        {"method": "ngram", "num_speculative_tokens": num_spec} if num_spec else None
+    )
+    vllm_config = EngineArgs(
+        model=model,
+        trust_remote_code=trust_remote_code,
+        skip_tokenizer_init=True,
+        speculative_config=speculative_config,
+    ).create_engine_config()
+    model_config = vllm_config.model_config
+    model_cls, _ = ModelRegistry.resolve_model_cls(
+        model_config.architecture, model_config=model_config
+    )
+    if (
+        not hasattr(model_cls, "get_mamba_state_copy_func")
+        # Models with several state layouts (e.g. Qwen4Exp) aren't modeled here.
+        or hasattr(model_cls, "get_mamba_specs_from_config")
+        or model_cls.get_mamba_state_copy_func()
+        != (get_conv_copy_spec, get_temporal_copy_spec)
+    ):
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"{model} ({model_config.architecture}) has no single conv + "
+            "temporal mamba state layout"
+        )
+
+    conv_shape, temporal_shape = model_cls.get_mamba_state_shape_from_config(
+        vllm_config
+    )
+    conv_dtype, temporal_dtype = model_cls.get_mamba_state_dtype_from_config(
+        vllm_config
+    )
+    if is_conv_state_dim_first():
+        conv_dim, conv_state_len = conv_shape
+    else:
+        conv_state_len, conv_dim = conv_shape
+
+    # Older configs tag mamba layers "mamba"; Transformers 5 remaps them to
+    # "linear_attention", the tag GDN layers already use.
+    parallel_config = vllm_config.parallel_config
+    num_state_layers = model_config.get_num_layers_by_block_type(
+        parallel_config, "mamba"
+    ) or model_config.get_num_layers_by_block_type(parallel_config, "linear_attention")
+    if num_state_layers == 0:
+        raise ValueError(f"{model}: found no mamba or linear_attention layers")
+    total_layers = model_config.get_total_num_hidden_layers()
+    return ModelStateConfig(
+        name=model,
+        num_state_layers=num_state_layers,
+        conv_dim=conv_dim,
+        conv_state_len=conv_state_len,
+        temporal_shape=tuple(temporal_shape),
+        conv_dtype=conv_dtype,
+        temporal_dtype=temporal_dtype,
+        num_spec=num_spec,
+        layer_kind=model_config.architecture,
+        notes=f"{num_state_layers} state layers out of {total_layers}",
+    )
+
+
+# Each request gets its own src/dst block ids inside every state tensor so
+# concurrent copies never alias; the state tensors are sized to 2*num_reqs
+# blocks in bench_one. Cold L2 comes from the flush before each timed launch.
+SRC_COL = 0
+DST_COL = 1
+TOKEN_BIAS = 0
+
+COPY_BLOCK_SIZE = 1024
+DEFAULT_ITERS_WARMUP = 20
+DEFAULT_ITERS_TIMED = 200
+
+
+@triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["src_col", "dst_col", "token_bias", "num_reqs"])
+def bench_copy_mamba_state_block(
+    src_col,
+    dst_col,
+    token_bias,
+    block_table_ptrs_ptr,
+    block_table_stride_req: tl.int64,
+    state_base_addrs_ptr,
+    state_block_strides_ptr,
+    state_elem_sizes_ptr,
+    state_inner_sizes_ptr,
+    state_conv_widths_ptr,
+    state_group_indices_ptr,
+    state_dim_row_count_ptr,
+    state_dim_row_stride_ptr,
+    num_reqs,
+    COPY_BLOCK_SIZE: tl.constexpr,
+    CONV_STATE_DIM_FIRST: tl.constexpr,
+    TEMPORAL_TILES: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    """Minimal wrapper: run the copy body for every (batch, state, tile) program.
+
+    Grid: (num_reqs, total_states, TEMPORAL_TILES).
+    """
+    batch_idx = tl.program_id(0)
+    state_idx = tl.program_id(1)
+    tile_idx = tl.program_id(2)
+    if batch_idx >= num_reqs:
+        return
+    _copy_mamba_state_block(
+        state_idx,
+        batch_idx,
+        src_col,
+        dst_col,
+        token_bias,
+        block_table_ptrs_ptr,
+        block_table_stride_req,
+        state_base_addrs_ptr,
+        state_block_strides_ptr,
+        state_elem_sizes_ptr,
+        state_inner_sizes_ptr,
+        state_conv_widths_ptr,
+        state_group_indices_ptr,
+        state_dim_row_count_ptr,
+        state_dim_row_stride_ptr,
+        tile_idx,
+        COPY_BLOCK_SIZE,
+        CONV_STATE_DIM_FIRST,
+        TEMPORAL_TILES,
+    )
+
+
+def build_state_tensors(
+    model: ModelStateConfig, conv_state_dim_first: bool, num_blocks: int
+) -> dict[str, list[torch.Tensor]]:
+    """Allocate one conv and one temporal state tensor per state-carrying layer.
+
+    Returns each layer's `kv_cache` list ([conv, temporal]) keyed by layer
+    name. Random contents let `check_copy` tell copied blocks from stale ones.
+    """
+    conv_shape_per_block = (
+        (model.conv_dim, model.conv_state_len)
+        if conv_state_dim_first
+        else (model.conv_state_len, model.conv_dim)
+    )
+
+    layer_states: dict[str, list[torch.Tensor]] = {}
+    for i in range(model.num_state_layers):
+        conv = torch.randn(
+            (num_blocks, *conv_shape_per_block),
+            dtype=model.conv_dtype,
+            device=DEVICE,
+        )
+        temporal = torch.randn(
+            (num_blocks, *model.temporal_shape),
+            dtype=model.temporal_dtype,
+            device=DEVICE,
+        )
+        layer_states[f"layers.{i}.mixer"] = [conv, temporal]
+    return layer_states
+
+
+def build_gpu_context(
+    layer_states: dict[str, list[torch.Tensor]], block_table: torch.Tensor
+) -> MambaSpecDecodeGPUContext:
+    """Populate the copy metadata with the production MambaSpecDecodeGPUContext.
+
+    The context reads only each layer's `kv_cache`, so a namespace holding the
+    state tensors stands in for the attention layer in the forward context.
+    """
+    conv, temporal = next(iter(layer_states.values()))
+    spec = MambaSpec(
+        # Only the postprocess decision logic reads block_size.
+        block_size=16,
+        shapes=(tuple(conv.shape[1:]), tuple(temporal.shape[1:])),
+        dtypes=(conv.dtype, temporal.dtype),
+    )
+    layer_config = MambaManager.layer_config(spec, mamba_cache_mode="align")
+    kv_cache_config = KVCacheConfig(
+        num_blocks=conv.shape[0],
+        kv_cache_tensors=[],
+        kv_cache_groups=[
+            KVCacheGroup.from_layers(dict.fromkeys(layer_states, layer_config))
+        ],
+    )
+    copy_funcs = {spec.mamba_type: (get_conv_copy_spec, get_temporal_copy_spec)}
+    forward_context = {
+        name: SimpleNamespace(kv_cache=states) for name, states in layer_states.items()
+    }
+    ctx = MambaSpecDecodeGPUContext.create(
+        max_num_reqs=block_table.shape[0],
+        kv_cache_config=kv_cache_config,
+        copy_funcs=copy_funcs,
+        forward_context=forward_context,
+        device=block_table.device,
+    )
+    ctx.initialize_from_forward_context(
+        kv_cache_config, forward_context, copy_funcs, [block_table]
+    )
+    return ctx
+
+
+def check_copy(
+    layer_states: dict[str, list[torch.Tensor]], block_table: torch.Tensor
+) -> None:
+    """Assert every state's dst blocks match its src blocks.
+
+    With TOKEN_BIAS=0 both conv and temporal copies move whole blocks.
+    """
+    src = block_table[:, SRC_COL].long()
+    dst = block_table[:, DST_COL].long()
+    for name, states in layer_states.items():
+        for state_type_idx, state in enumerate(states):
+            assert torch.equal(state[dst], state[src]), (
+                f"{name} state {state_type_idx}: dst blocks differ from src"
+            )
+
+
+def bytes_moved_per_launch(
+    layer_states: dict[str, list[torch.Tensor]], conv_state_dim_first: bool
+) -> int:
+    """Bytes copied (read+write) across all (num_reqs, state, tile) programs,
+    per request. Multiply by num_reqs to get per-launch total."""
+    per_req = 0
+    for conv, temporal in layer_states.values():
+        elem = conv.element_size()
+        if conv_state_dim_first:
+            per_req += conv.size(1) * (conv.size(2) - TOKEN_BIAS) * elem
+        else:
+            per_req += (conv.size(1) - TOKEN_BIAS) * conv.stride(1) * elem
+        per_req += temporal[0].numel() * temporal.element_size()
+    return per_req
+
+
+def bench_one(
+    model: ModelStateConfig,
+    num_reqs: int,
+    temporal_tiles: int,
+    iters_warmup: int,
+    iters_timed: int,
+) -> None:
+    # The production metadata reads the conv layout from the env, so the
+    # allocation and the CONV_STATE_DIM_FIRST constexpr follow it too.
+    conv_state_dim_first = is_conv_state_dim_first()
+    # Give every request distinct src/dst block ids so concurrent copies don't
+    # share cache lines. State tensors hold at least 2*num_reqs blocks.
+    num_blocks = 2 * num_reqs
+    layer_states = build_state_tensors(model, conv_state_dim_first, num_blocks)
+
+    # Single mamba group. Per-request rows point to distinct src/dst blocks:
+    # req i reads block 2*i and writes block 2*i+1. Two columns are enough
+    # since token_bias=0 (no extra columns read by the temporal path).
+    block_table = torch.zeros(num_reqs, 2, dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE)
+    row_ids = torch.arange(num_reqs, dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE)
+    block_table[:, SRC_COL] = 2 * row_ids
+    block_table[:, DST_COL] = 2 * row_ids + 1
+    ctx = build_gpu_context(layer_states, block_table)
+
+    grid = (num_reqs, ctx.num_states, temporal_tiles)
+    args = (
+        SRC_COL,
+        DST_COL,
+        TOKEN_BIAS,
+        ctx.block_table_ptrs,
+        ctx.block_table_stride_req,
+        ctx.state_base_addrs,
+        ctx.state_block_strides,
+        ctx.state_elem_sizes,
+        ctx.state_inner_sizes,
+        ctx.state_conv_widths,
+        ctx.state_group_indices,
+        ctx.state_dim_row_count,
+        ctx.state_dim_row_stride,
+        num_reqs,
+    )
+
+    def launch():
+        bench_copy_mamba_state_block[grid](
+            *args,
+            COPY_BLOCK_SIZE=COPY_BLOCK_SIZE,
+            CONV_STATE_DIM_FIRST=conv_state_dim_first,
+            TEMPORAL_TILES=temporal_tiles,
+        )
+
+    launch()
+    torch.accelerator.synchronize()
+    check_copy(layer_states, block_table)
+
+    layout = "DS" if conv_state_dim_first else "SD"
+    # Underscore separator: '/' is Nsight's NVTX level marker and breaks
+    # --nvtx-include filters when it appears inside a range name.
+    label = f"reqs={num_reqs}_conv={layout}_tiles={temporal_tiles}"
+    nvtx.range_push(label)
+    # Not use_cuda_graph: its no-CUPTI fallback keeps L2 cold by cloning tensor
+    # args, which can't relocate states reached through raw metadata pointers.
+    times_ms = bench_gpu_time_with_cupti(
+        launch,
+        dry_run_iters=iters_warmup,
+        repeat_iters=iters_timed,
+        cold_l2_cache=True,
+        use_cuda_graph=False,
+    )
+    nvtx.range_pop()
+
+    median_us = statistics.median(times_ms) * 1000.0
+    bytes_per_req = bytes_moved_per_launch(layer_states, conv_state_dim_first)
+    total_bytes = bytes_per_req * num_reqs
+    # Read + write: memory traffic is 2x copy size.
+    gbps = (2 * total_bytes) / (median_us * 1e-6) / 1e9
+    print(
+        f"{label:30s} grid={grid!s:16s} "
+        f"copy/req={bytes_per_req / 1024 / 1024:6.2f} MiB  "
+        f"median={median_us:8.2f} us  BW~{gbps:6.1f} GB/s"
+    )
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--model",
+        default=_QWEN3_5_9B.name,
+        help=(
+            "HF model whose state layout drives the benchmark. Preset names "
+            "(see --list-models) work offline; others fetch the HF config."
+        ),
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--list-models",
+        action="store_true",
+        help="List offline preset names for --model and exit.",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--num-spec",
+        type=int,
+        default=None,
+        help=(
+            "Speculative tokens, which lengthen the conv state. Default: the "
+            "preset's value, or the MTP layer count in the HF config."
+        ),
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--trust-remote-code",
+        action="store_true",
+        help="Trust remote code when loading the HF config.",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--concurrencies",
+        type=int,
+        nargs="+",
+        default=[1, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128],
+        help="num_reqs values to sweep (default matches serving benchmark)",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--conv-layout",
+        choices=["SD", "DS", "both"],
+        default="SD",
+        help="Conv state layout to benchmark. Real Qwen3.5-9B is SD.",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--temporal-tiles",
+        type=int,
+        nargs="+",
+        default=[_TEMPORAL_TILES],
+        help="TEMPORAL_TILES values to sweep (default: production value).",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--iters-warmup",
+        type=int,
+        default=DEFAULT_ITERS_WARMUP,
+        help="Untimed launches before CUPTI timing.",
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--iters-timed",
+        type=int,
+        default=DEFAULT_ITERS_TIMED,
+        help=(
+            "CUPTI-timed launches per config, each after an L2 flush; the "
+            "median is reported."
+        ),
+    )
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+
+    if args.list_models:
+        for name in sorted(MODEL_CONFIGS.keys()):
+            print(name)
+        return
+
+    assert torch.cuda.is_available(), "CUDA required"
+    model = MODEL_CONFIGS.get(args.model)
+    if model is None:
+        model = model_state_config_from_hf(
+            args.model, args.num_spec, args.trust_remote_code
+        )
+    elif args.num_spec is not None:
+        model = replace(
+            model,
+            num_spec=args.num_spec,
+            conv_state_len=model.conv_state_len - model.num_spec + args.num_spec,
+        )
+    conv_elem = torch.tensor([], dtype=model.conv_dtype).element_size()
+    temp_elem = torch.tensor([], dtype=model.temporal_dtype).element_size()
+    conv_bytes_per_block = model.conv_dim * model.conv_state_len * conv_elem
+    temp_inner = math.prod(model.temporal_shape)
+    temp_bytes_per_block = temp_inner * temp_elem
+
+    print(f"device: {torch.cuda.get_device_name(0)}")
+    print(
+        f"model: {model.name} ({model.layer_kind}) tp=1 num_spec={model.num_spec}\n"
+        f"state_layers={model.num_state_layers} state_types=2 "
+        f"total_states={model.total_states}  # {model.notes}\n"
+        f"conv: dim={model.conv_dim} state_len={model.conv_state_len} "
+        f"dtype={model.conv_dtype} "
+        f"(={conv_bytes_per_block / 1024:.1f} KiB/block)\n"
+        f"temporal: shape={model.temporal_shape} inner={temp_inner} "
+        f"dtype={model.temporal_dtype} "
+        f"(={temp_bytes_per_block / 1024 / 1024:.2f} MiB/block)\n"
+        f"iters warmup={args.iters_warmup} timed={args.iters_timed}"
+    )
+    print()
+
+    layouts = ["SD", "DS"] if args.conv_layout == "both" else [args.conv_layout]
+
+    torch.cuda.cudart().cudaProfilerStart()
+    t0 = time.perf_counter()
+    for layout in layouts:
+        os.environ["VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT"] = layout
+        get_conv_state_layout.cache_clear()
+        for tiles in args.temporal_tiles:
+            for nr in args.concurrencies:
+                bench_one(model, nr, tiles, args.iters_warmup, args.iters_timed)
+    torch.cuda.cudart().cudaProfilerStop()
+    print(f"\ntotal wall: {time.perf_counter() - t0:.2f}s")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+    # Compact the kept prefix in one pass. These markers cannot overlap, so
+    # deleting each suffix as it completes also removes markers formed by
+    # earlier deletions, without rescanning the text.
+    buffer = bytearray(text, "utf-8", errors="surrogatepass")

+                    kept -= len(marker)

+    del buffer[kept:]

Signed-off-by: Bugen Zhao <i@bugenzhao.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-authored-by: vllm-agent <claw@inferact.ai>

[Rust Frontend] Accept Python's inverse spellings of boolean flags (#70096)

Signed-off-by: Bugen Zhao <i@bugenzhao.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-authored-by: vllm-agent <claw@inferact.ai>

[Rust Frontend] Bound allowed_token_ids by the model vocabulary (#70093)

Signed-off-by: Bugen Zhao <i@bugenzhao.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-authored-by: vllm-agent <claw@inferact.ai>

[Rust Frontend] Resolve parser selections at model load and refuse unusable explicit ones (#69614)

Signed-off-by: Bugen Zhao <i@bugenzhao.com>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Co-authored-by: vllm-agent <claw@inferact.ai>

+    warn_if_rust_frontend_stale(_binary(checkout / "vllm", _version(built)))

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Detect a packaged `vllm-rs` binary that lacks the checkout's `rust/` sources.
+
+Precompiled installs (`VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1` or
+`VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED_RUST=1`) take `vllm-rs` from the wheel of an upstream
+main commit, so `rust/` changes on a local branch are never built, and an
+editable install keeps the old binary across `git pull`. The check warns only
+on clear evidence and stays silent whenever the evidence is missing.
+"""
+
+import os
+import subprocess
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+import regex as re
+
+import vllm
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+# The setuptools-scm local version: `+g<commit>` for a clean tree, followed by
+# `.dYYYYMMDD` when built from a dirty one.
+_VERSION_COMMIT_RE = re.compile(r"\+g([0-9a-f]{7,40})(\.d\d{8})?$")
+_SUBPROCESS_TIMEOUT_S = 10
+_MAX_LISTED_PATHS = 5
+
+
+@dataclass
+class UnbuiltRustChanges:
+    checkout: str
+    binary_commit: str
+    changed_paths: list[str]
+
+
+def _run(args: list[str], env: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> str | None:
+    try:
+        result = subprocess.run(
+            args,
+            capture_output=True,
+            text=True,
+            timeout=_SUBPROCESS_TIMEOUT_S,
+            check=True,
+            env=env,
+            errors="replace",
+        )
+    except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError):
+        return None
+    return result.stdout.strip()
+
+
+def find_unbuilt_rust_changes(
+    binary_path: str, package_dir: str
+) -> UnbuiltRustChanges | None:
+    """Return the `rust/` changes the packaged `binary_path` was not built with.
+
+    Returns None unless `package_dir` is the `vllm/` directory of a git
+    checkout, `binary_path` is the `vllm-rs` packaged next to it (possibly a
+    symlink), and the binary reports a clean commit that the checkout has.
+    """
+    package_dir = os.path.realpath(package_dir)
+    # A binary chosen through VLLM_RUST_FRONTEND_PATH has its own provenance.
+    if (
+        os.path.basename(binary_path) != "vllm-rs"
+        or os.path.realpath(os.path.dirname(binary_path)) != package_dir
+    ):
+        return None
+
+    # Stay local: no lazy fetches in partial clones, no index refresh writes.
+    git_env = {**os.environ, "GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH": "1", "GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS": "0"}
+    checkout = _run(["git", "-C", package_dir, "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"], git_env)
+    if checkout is None:
+        return None
+    # A non-editable install inside a checkout (e.g. a venv in the repo) does
+    # not run the checkout's sources.
+    if os.path.realpath(os.path.join(checkout, "vllm")) != package_dir:
+        return None
+
+    version = _run([binary_path, "--version"])
+    match = _VERSION_COMMIT_RE.search(version.split()[-1]) if version else None
+    if match is None or match.group(2) is not None:
+        return None
+    reported = match.group(1)
+
+    git = ["git", "-C", checkout]
+    binary_commit = _run(
+        [*git, "rev-parse", "--verify", "--quiet", f"{reported}^{{commit}}"], git_env
+    )
+    # `rev-parse` prefers a ref with the same name over an abbreviated hash.
+    if binary_commit is None or not binary_commit.startswith(reported):
+        return None
+    changed = _run([*git, "diff", "--name-only", binary_commit, "--", "rust/"], git_env)
+    if changed is None:
+        return None
+    # Cargo also builds untracked files it discovers, such as a new `build.rs`.
+    untracked = _run(
+        [*git, "ls-files", "--others", "--exclude-standard", "--", "rust/"], git_env
+    )
+    paths = changed.splitlines() + (untracked or "").splitlines()
+    if not paths:
+        return None
+    return UnbuiltRustChanges(checkout, binary_commit, paths)
+
+
+def warn_if_rust_frontend_stale(binary_path: str) -> None:
+    """Warn when the packaged `vllm-rs` was built without this checkout's
+    `rust/` changes."""
+    package_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(vllm.__file__))
+    unbuilt = find_unbuilt_rust_changes(binary_path, package_dir)
+    if unbuilt is None:
+        return
+
+    paths = unbuilt.changed_paths
+    listed = ", ".join(paths[:_MAX_LISTED_PATHS])
+    if len(paths) > _MAX_LISTED_PATHS:
+        listed += ", ..."
+    files = "1 file" if len(paths) == 1 else f"{len(paths)} files"
+    logger.warning(
+        "The Rust frontend binary %s was built from commit %s, but rust/ in %s "
+        "differs from that commit in %s (%s). The binary was not rebuilt after "
+        "local edits or a checkout update, or it came from an install with "
+        "VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED=1 or VLLM_USE_PRECOMPILED_RUST=1 on a branch that "
+        "changes rust/. It may not match this checkout's Python code, so the "
+        "server can fail at startup or on requests, or return wrong results. "
+        "Rebuild it with `./tools/build_rust.sh`.",
+        binary_path,
+        unbuilt.binary_commit[:10],
+        unbuilt.checkout,
+        files,
+        listed,
+    )

+"""Error bounds for helpers that cannot be bit-exact.
+
+The bounds are derived from the ISA's documented accuracy and from the
+arithmetic each helper performs, not measured from the kernel they check.
+They are shared so that every model's tests are bounded the same way.
+The one exception is `_FP8_BLOCK_PRECISION`, an empirical envelope.
+
+ISA references:
+- CDNA3: https://www.amd.com/content/dam/amd/en/documents/instinct-tech-docs/instruction-set-architectures/amd-instinct-mi300-cdna3-instruction-set-architecture.pdf
+- CDNA4: https://www.amd.com/content/dam/amd/en/documents/instinct-tech-docs/instruction-set-architectures/amd-instinct-cdna4-instruction-set-architecture.pdf
+"""
+
+import torch
+
+from tests.models.common.specialized_decode import reference as R
+
+# Unit roundoff of float32 (half an ulp at 1): the relative error of one
+# round-to-nearest operation.
+F32_ROUNDOFF = 2.0**-24
+
+# The ISA documents V_EXP_F32, V_LOG_F32, V_RSQ_F32 and V_RCP_F32 as accurate
+# to 1 ulp, with denormal results flushed to zero.
+TRANSCENDENTAL_RELATIVE = 2 * F32_ROUNDOFF
+TRANSCENDENTAL_FLUSH = R.FLT_MIN
+
+
+def transcendental_bound(reference: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Allowed error of a hardware transcendental: 1 ulp of `reference`, or
+    the whole result where it may be flushed to zero.
+
+    The flush region starts just above `FLT_MIN`, because a result there may
+    round down to a denormal and then be flushed.
+    """
+    return torch.where(
+        reference.abs() < TRANSCENDENTAL_FLUSH * (1 + TRANSCENDENTAL_RELATIVE),
+        TRANSCENDENTAL_FLUSH,
+        R.ulp(reference, torch.float32),
+    )
+
+
+# Empirical, not derived: the gfx950 FP8 MFMA sums each K block at the
+# precision of the block's largest product, and the ISA does not say how much
+# that drops. The measured error of `test_mfma_scaled` is 0.20-0.24 of the
+# resulting bound.
+_FP8_BLOCK_PRECISION = 2.0**-14
+
+
+class RoundingModel:
+    """First-order rounding error of a float32 formula, computed by autograd.
+
+    Evaluate the formula in float64 and wrap each float32 operation in a call
+    to the instance, which models it as `value * (1 + relative) + absolute`.
+    `bound` then returns `sum_i |d result / d e_i| * |e_i|` over those error
+    terms. Second-order terms are ignored.
+
+    Only elementwise formulas are supported, since the gradient is taken of
+    `result.sum()`.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        # (error term, its maximum magnitude)
+        self._perturbations: list[tuple[torch.Tensor, float]] = []
+
+    def __call__(
+        self,
+        value: torch.Tensor,
+        relative: float = F32_ROUNDOFF,
+        absolute: float = 0.0,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        """Model one operation with the given relative and absolute error.
+        The defaults are a correctly rounded float32 operation."""
+        relative_term = torch.zeros_like(value, requires_grad=True)
+        self._perturbations.append((relative_term, relative))
+        value = value * (1 + relative_term)
+        # Skipped when zero to save autograd memory on large inputs.
+        if absolute:
+            absolute_term = torch.zeros_like(value, requires_grad=True)
+            self._perturbations.append((absolute_term, absolute))
+            value = value + absolute_term
+        return value
+
+    def transcendental(self, value: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        """Model a 1-ulp, flush-to-zero hardware transcendental."""
+        return self(value, TRANSCENDENTAL_RELATIVE, TRANSCENDENTAL_FLUSH)
+
+    def bound(self, result: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        """Maximum error of `result` from the exact formula."""
+        assert self._perturbations, "the formula went through no rounding"
+        assert all(term.shape == result.shape for term, _ in self._perturbations), (
+            "elementwise formulas only: a rounding whose shape differs from "
+            "the result's means the formula reduced across elements"
+        )
+        gradients = torch.autograd.grad(
+            result.sum(), [term for term, _ in self._perturbations]
+        )
+        total = torch.zeros_like(gradients[0])
+        for (_, size), gradient in zip(self._perturbations, gradients):
+            total = total + size * gradient.abs()
+        return total
+
+
+def _block_max_products(a: torch.Tensor, b: torch.Tensor, block: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Sum over K blocks of `max_k |a_k b_k|`, for `a` `[..., M, K]` and
+    `b` `[..., N, K]`."""
+    a, b = a.double().abs(), b.double().abs()
+    total = torch.zeros(*a.shape[:-1], b.shape[-2], dtype=R.F64, device=a.device)
+    for k in range(0, a.shape[-1], block):
+        a_block, b_block = a[..., k : k + block], b[..., k : k + block]
+        total = total + (a_block.unsqueeze(-2) * b_block.unsqueeze(-3)).amax(-1)
+    return total
+
+
+def mfma_accumulation_bound(
+    a: torch.Tensor,
+    b: torch.Tensor,
+    acc: torch.Tensor,
+    block: int | None = None,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Worst-case error of an MFMA computing `D = C + A B^T` with fp32
+    accumulation over K: `(K + 1) 2^-24 (|C| + |A| |B|^T)`.
+
+    Products of bf16 or fp8 operands are exact in fp32, so only the adds
+    round. For FP8 MFMAs, pass `block` to add the block-sum term
+    `block * _FP8_BLOCK_PRECISION * sum_blocks max_k |a_k b_k|`.
+
+    Args:
+        a: Dequantized float64 operand, `[..., M, K]`.
+        b: Dequantized float64 operand, `[..., N, K]`.
+        acc: Accumulator input C, `[..., M, N]`.
+        block: FP8 K-block size, or None for an fp32 accumulation.
+
+    """
+    bound = (
+        (a.shape[-1] + 1)
+        * F32_ROUNDOFF
+        * (acc.abs() + a.abs() @ b.abs().transpose(-1, -2))
+    )
+    if block is not None:
+        bound = bound + block * _FP8_BLOCK_PRECISION * _block_max_products(a, b, block)
+    return bound

+# ------------------------------------------------- MFMA operands and layouts
+# Lane layouts of the CDNA MFMA operands, as documented in the ISA.
+
+# Operand format codes of the f8f6f4 MFMA (CDNA4 ISA).
+MX_FP8, MX_FP4 = 0, 4
+
+
+def mfma_lanes(tile: torch.Tensor, per_lane: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """[tiles, 16, K] -> the [tiles 64, per_lane] lane operands of a 16 x 16
+    MFMA: lane l holds row l % 16, K per_lane (l / 16) .. + per_lane."""
+    tiles = tile.shape[0]
+    return (
+        tile.view(tiles, 16, 4, per_lane)
+        .permute(0, 2, 1, 3)
+        .reshape(tiles * 64, per_lane)
+    )
+
+
+def acc_lanes(acc: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """[tiles, 16, 16] accumulator -> the [tiles 64, 4] lane operands: lane l
+    holds rows 4 (l / 16) .. + 3 of column l % 16."""
+    return acc.view(-1, 4, 4, 16).transpose(2, 3).reshape(-1, 4)
+
+
+def from_acc_lanes(lanes: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """`acc_lanes` undone: [tiles 64, 4] -> [tiles, 16, 16]."""
+    return lanes.view(-1, 4, 16, 4).transpose(2, 3).reshape(-1, 16, 16)
+

+def _fp8_mfma_lanes(quantized: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """[tiles, 16, 128] E4M3 -> the f8f6f4 MFMA's lane operands: lane l holds
+    row l % 16, K 16 j .. + 16 and 64 + 16 j .. + 16, for j = l / 16."""
+    tiles = quantized.shape[0]
+    halves = quantized.view(tiles, 16, 2, 4, 16).permute(0, 3, 1, 2, 4)
+    return halves.reshape(tiles * 64, 32).contiguous()

+    """Operands of a 16 x 16 x 32 bf16 MFMA, as matrices rather than lanes."""

+    b: torch.Tensor  # [tiles, 16, 32] bfloat16
+    acc: torch.Tensor  # [tiles, 16, 16] float32

+def _wide_bf16(
+    shape: tuple[int, ...], exponents: tuple[int, int], g: torch.Generator
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    x = torch.randn(shape, device=DEV, generator=g)

+    return (x * spread).bfloat16()

+def wide_bf16(
+    shape: tuple[int, ...], exponents: tuple[int, int], seed: int

+    """bf16 normals of `shape` scaled by random powers of two in `exponents`,
+    so that a float32 accumulation of them actually rounds."""

+    the exact unscaled operands in float64."""

+    a_words: torch.Tensor  # [tiles 64, n] int32 lane operands
+    b_words: torch.Tensor
+    a_values: torch.Tensor  # [tiles, 16, 128] float64
+    b_values: torch.Tensor

+    scale_codes: torch.Tensor  # [2, tiles 64, 4], the codes those words hold
+    acc: torch.Tensor  # [tiles, 16, 16] float32

+def _mx_operand(
+    tiles: int, fmt: int, g: torch.Generator

+    """Random MXFP8 (no NaN) or MXFP4 `[tiles, 16, 128]` -> (lane words,

+def wave_butterfly(
+    values: torch.Tensor, offsets: tuple[int, ...], op: str

+    """Lane-xor butterfly reduction of `values` (float32, whole waves) with
+    `op` ('add' or 'max'): for each offset in order, lane l combines with lane

+        copies={"dsv41": ops.hw_rsq, "dsv41_attn": attn.hw_rsq},
+    ),
+    "sigmoid": _Transcendental(
+        inputs=lambda count, seed: [I.mixed_floats(count, -80, 80, _SMALL, seed)],
+        reference=torch.sigmoid,
+        rounding=_sigmoid_rounding,
+        copies={"dsv41": seam.sigmoid},
+    ),
+    "_score": _Transcendental(
+        # 20 and its neighbours: where softplus switches to returning x.
+        inputs=lambda count, seed: [
+            torch.cat(
+                [
+                    I.mixed_floats(count - 3, -40, 40, _SMALL, seed),
+                    I.neighbours(torch.full((1,), 20.0, device=DEV)),
+                ]
+            )
+        ],
+        reference=R.sqrt_softplus_score,
+        rounding=_score_rounding,
+        copies={"dsv41": moe._score},
+        measured=torch.square,
+    ),
+}
+
+
+def _transcendental_cases() -> list[Any]:
+    return [
+        pytest.param(lib, name, id=f"{lib}-{name}")
+        for name, case in _TRANSCENDENTALS.items()
+        for lib in case.copies
+    ]
+
+
+def _transcendental_error(lib: str, name: str, seed: int, count: int) -> float:
+    """The largest error of helper `name` of `lib` over `count` inputs, as a
+    fraction of its bound."""
+    case = _TRANSCENDENTALS[name]
+    helper = case.copies[lib]
+    columns = case.inputs(count, seed)
+    got = _run(
+        f"t_{lib}_{name}", lambda *w: [H.i32(helper(*map(H.f32, w)))], 1, *columns
+    )
+    result = got.view(F32)[:, 0].double()
+    exact = [column.double() for column in columns]
+    reference = case.reference(*exact)
+    if case.measured is not None:
+        result, reference = case.measured(result), case.measured(reference)
+    if case.rounding is None:
+        return (
+            ((result - reference).abs() / B.transcendental_bound(reference))
+            .max()
+            .item()
+        )
+    rounding = B.RoundingModel()
+    modelled = case.rounding(rounding, *exact)
+    # The bound is the rounding error plus the gap between the helper's exact
+    # formula and the reference, which are different expressions.
+    rounding_bound = rounding.bound(modelled)
+    formula_gap = (modelled.detach() - reference).abs()
+    # Keep the formula gap negligible (checked per element) so it can't hide
+    # a wrong rounding model. Measured on gfx950: ~2e-9.
+    worst = (formula_gap / rounding_bound).nan_to_num().max()
+    assert worst <= 1e-3, (
+        f"{name}: the modelled formula is {worst:.3g} of the rounding bound "
+        f"from the reference, which is too much of it to stay negligible"
+    )
+    bound = formula_gap + rounding_bound
+    # Exact results pass even where the bound is zero.
+    error = torch.where(result == reference, 0.0, (result - reference).abs() / bound)
+    return error.max().item()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(("lib", "name"), _transcendental_cases())
+def test_transcendentals(lib: str, name: str) -> None:
+    """Hardware transcendentals within 1 ulp of float64 torch, and helpers
+    built on them within their rounding bound, over 2^22 inputs."""
+    error = _transcendental_error(lib, name, seed=0, count=1 << 22)
+    assert error <= 1, f"{name}: {error:.3g} of its bound"
+
+
+_DIV_RN: dict[str, H.DeviceFn] = {"dsv41": ops.div_rn, "dsv41_attn": attn.div_rn}
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("lib", _DIV_RN)
+def test_div_rn(lib: str) -> None:
+    """div_rn(x, d, RN(1 / d)) returns the correctly rounded quotient."""
+    div_rn = _DIV_RN[lib]
+    count = 1 << 22
+    # One draw split in two, so numerator and denominator differ.
+    drawn = I.log_uniform(2 * count, -60, 60, seed=3)
+    numerator, denominator = drawn[:count], drawn[count:]
+    # Rounding the f64 quotient to f32 is exact here (53 >= 2 * 24 + 2 bits).
+    reciprocal = 1 / denominator
+    got = _run(
+        f"div_{lib}",
+        lambda *w: [H.i32(div_rn(*map(H.f32, w)))],
+        1,
+        numerator,
+        denominator,
+        reciprocal,
+    )
+    quotient = R.f32_rne(numerator.double() / denominator.double())
+    I.assert_bit_exact(got[:, 0], I.bits(quotient), "div_rn", numerator)
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- reductions
+_BUTTERFLY: dict[str, H.DeviceFn] = {
+    "dsv41": ops.butterfly,
+    "dsv41_attn": attn.butterfly,
+}
+_BUTTERFLY_OPS: dict[str, Callable[[Any, Any], Any]] = {
+    "add": lambda a, b: a + b,
+    "max": fx.max,
+}
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("op", ["add", "max"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("offsets", [(32, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1), (16, 8, 4, 2, 1)])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("lib", _BUTTERFLY)
+def test_butterfly(lib: str, offsets: tuple[int, ...], op: str) -> None:
+    """butterfly(v, offsets, op) reduces in exactly the documented order."""
+    butterfly = _BUTTERFLY[lib]
+    combine = _BUTTERFLY_OPS[op]
+    values = I.log_uniform(R.WAVE * 4096, -20, 20, seed=4)
+    got = _run(
+        f"bfly_{lib}_{''.join(map(str, offsets))}_{op}",
+        lambda w: [H.i32(butterfly(H.f32(w), offsets, combine))],
+        1,
+        values,
+    )
+    folded = R.wave_butterfly(values, offsets, op)
+    I.assert_bit_exact(got[:, 0], folded.view(I32), "butterfly", values)
+    if op == "add":
+        # The inputs must be sensitive to the order for the test to check it.
+        other_order = R.wave_butterfly(values, offsets[::-1], op)
+        assert not torch.equal(folded, other_order), "inputs blind to the order"
+
+
+_SUM_PARTIALS: dict[str, H.DeviceFn] = {"dsv41": ops.sum_partials}
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("tp", [2, 4, 8])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("lib", _SUM_PARTIALS)
+def test_sum_partials(lib: str, tp: int) -> None:
+    """sum_partials sums the ranks' bf16 pair partials in float32 in rank
+    order, bit for bit. The order check needs `tp >= 3`."""
+    sum_partials = _SUM_PARTIALS[lib]
+    partials = I.wide_bf16((1 << 16, tp, 2), (-8, 8), seed=5)
+
+    def body(*words: Any) -> list[Any]:
+        polled = [[words[rank]] for rank in range(tp)]
+        return [
+            H.i32(x) for x in sum_partials(lambda reqs: polled, None, lambda s: s, tp)
+        ]
+
+    got = _run(f"sp_{lib}_{tp}", body, 2, partials.view(-1, tp * 2).view(I32))
+    in_order = partials[:, 0].float()
+    for rank in range(1, tp):
+        in_order = in_order + partials[:, rank].float()
+    I.assert_bit_exact(got.view(F32), in_order, "sum_partials", partials.float().sum(1))
+    backwards = partials.float().flip(1)
+    reversed_order = backwards[:, 0]
+    for rank in range(1, tp):
+        reversed_order = reversed_order + backwards[:, rank]
+    assert tp == 2 or not torch.equal(in_order, reversed_order), (
+        "inputs blind to the rank order"
+    )
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------- MFMA
+def _mfma_error(
+    lanes: torch.Tensor,
+    a: torch.Tensor,
+    b: torch.Tensor,
+    acc: torch.Tensor,
+    block: int | None = None,
+) -> float:
+    """Error of the MFMA result `lanes` for `D = C + A B^T`, as a fraction of
+    `B.mfma_accumulation_bound`."""
+    product = I.from_acc_lanes(lanes.view(F32).double())
+    reference = acc + a @ b.transpose(1, 2)
+    bound = B.mfma_accumulation_bound(a, b, acc, block)
+    return ((product - reference).abs() / bound).max().item()
+
+
+_MFMA_BF16: dict[str, H.DeviceFn] = {
+    "dsv41": ops.mfma_bf16,
+    "dsv41_attn": attn.mfma_bf16,
+    # gfx942 emulation from two 16 x 16 x 16 MFMAs.
+    "dsv41-k32": gfx.mfma_bf16_k32,
+}
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("variant", _MFMA_BF16)
+def test_mfma_bf16(variant: str) -> None:
+    """The 16 x 16 x 32 bf16 MFMA against the float64 product."""
+    mfma = _MFMA_BF16[variant]
+    a, b, acc = I.bf16_mfma_operands(256, seed=7)
+
+    def body(*words: Any) -> list[Any]:
+        operands = [
+            fx.Vector.from_elements(list(words[i : i + 4]), fx.Int32) for i in (0, 4)
+        ]
+        accumulator = fx.Vector.from_elements([H.f32(w) for w in words[8:]], fx.Float32)
+        d = mfma(
+            operands[0].bitcast(fx.BFloat16),
+            operands[1].bitcast(fx.BFloat16),
+            accumulator,
+        )
+        return [H.i32(d[i]) for i in range(4)]
+
+    lanes = [I.mfma_lanes(t, 8).contiguous().view(I32) for t in (a, b)]
+    # Kernel names cannot contain "-".
+    got = _run(f"mfma_{variant.replace('-', '_')}", body, 4, *lanes, I.acc_lanes(acc))
+    error = _mfma_error(got, a.double(), b.double(), acc.double())
+    assert error <= 1, f"{error:.3g} of the fp32 accumulation bound"
+
+
+class _ScaledMfma(NamedTuple):
+    """A scaled MFMA implementation and the cases to test it on."""
+
+    mfma: H.DeviceFn
+    # (A, B) operand formats used by callers.
+    formats: tuple[tuple[int, int], ...]
+    # Scale-word byte for A and for B.
+    selectors: tuple[tuple[int, int], ...]
+    # False if the wrapper hard-codes byte 0 and takes no selector arguments.
+    takes_selectors: bool
+
+
+_MFMA_SCALED: dict[str, _ScaledMfma] = {
+    "dsv41": _ScaledMfma(
+        mfma=mx.mfma_scaled,
+        formats=((mx.FP8, mx.FP8), (mx.FP4, mx.FP8), (mx.FP4, mx.FP4)),
+        selectors=((0, 0), (1, 2), (3, 1)),
+        takes_selectors=True,
+    ),
+    "dsv41_attn": _ScaledMfma(
+        mfma=attn.mfma_scaled,
+        formats=((attn.FP8, attn.FP8),),
+        selectors=((0, 0),),
+        takes_selectors=False,
+    ),
+}
+
+# The same check for the bounded helpers.
+for _copies in (
+    *(case.copies for case in _TRANSCENDENTALS.values()),
+    _DIV_RN,
+    _BUTTERFLY,
+    _MFMA_BF16,
+    {lib: spec.mfma for lib, spec in _MFMA_SCALED.items()},
+):
+    if "dsv41_attn" in _copies:
+        assert _copies["dsv41"] is not _copies["dsv41_attn"], (
+            "the two copies now share a helper"
+        )
+
+
+def _scaled_cases() -> list[Any]:
+    out = []
+    for lib, spec in _MFMA_SCALED.items():
+        for formats in spec.formats:
+            names = "x".join("fp4" if fmt else "fp8" for fmt in formats)
+            for selector in spec.selectors:
+                out.append(
+                    pytest.param(lib, formats, selector, id=f"{lib}-{names}-{selector}")
+                )
+    return out
+
+
+def _scaled_mfma_error(
+    lib: str,
+    formats: tuple[int, int],
+    selector: tuple[int, int],
+    seed: int,
+    tiles: int,
+) -> tuple[float, float]:
+    """Run the scaled MFMA of `lib` on random operands. Returns the error as a
+    fraction of the full bound and of the fp32-only bound."""
+    spec = _MFMA_SCALED[lib]
+    operands = I.mx_mfma_operands(tiles, formats, seed)
+    a_words, b_words = operands.a_words, operands.b_words
+    a_count, b_count = a_words.shape[1], b_words.shape[1]
+    extra = selector if spec.takes_selectors else ()
+
+    def body(*words: Any) -> list[Any]:
+        a = fx.Vector.from_elements(list(words[:a_count]), fx.Int32)
+        b = fx.Vector.from_elements(list(words[a_count : a_count + b_count]), fx.Int32)
+        accumulator = fx.Vector.from_elements(
+            [H.f32(w) for w in words[a_count + b_count : -2]], fx.Float32
+        )
+        d = spec.mfma(a, b, accumulator, words[-2], words[-1], *formats, *extra)
+        return [H.i32(d[i]) for i in range(4)]
+
+    got = _run(
+        f"mfs_{lib}_{formats[0]}{formats[1]}_{selector[0]}{selector[1]}",
+        body,
+        4,
+        a_words,
+        b_words,
+        I.acc_lanes(operands.acc),
+        operands.scale_words[0],
+        operands.scale_words[1],
+    )
+
+    def scaled(values: torch.Tensor, side: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+        """`values` `[tiles, 16, 128]` times its selected K-block scale."""
+        code = operands.scale_codes[side, :, selector[side]]
+        scale = R.e8m0(code.view(tiles, 4, 16).transpose(1, 2))
+        return values * scale.repeat_interleave(32, -1)
+
+    a = scaled(operands.a_values, 0)
+    b = scaled(operands.b_values, 1)
+    # FP4 x FP4 products span at most 12^2 = 144, so the block sum loses
+    # nothing and needs no block term.
+    block = None if formats == (I.MX_FP4, I.MX_FP4) else 32
+    acc = operands.acc.double()
+    return _mfma_error(got, a, b, acc, block), _mfma_error(got, a, b, acc)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(GFX942, reason="the scaled f8f6f4 MFMA is gfx950 only")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(("lib", "formats", "selector"), _scaled_cases())
+def test_mfma_scaled(
+    lib: str, formats: tuple[int, int], selector: tuple[int, int]
+) -> None:
+    """The 16 x 16 x 128 scaled MFMA (f8f6f4) against the float64 product of
+    the dequantized operands.
+
+    The FP8 bound is dominated by the empirical `B._FP8_BLOCK_PRECISION`, so
+    this checks the instruction is wired correctly rather than its precision.
+    """
+    error, fp32_only = _scaled_mfma_error(lib, formats, selector, seed=8, tiles=256)
+    assert error <= 1, f"{error:.3g} of the bound"
+    if formats != (I.MX_FP4, I.MX_FP4):
+        # The block term must be needed: the error should far exceed the
+        # fp32-only bound (25-49x on gfx950).
+        assert fp32_only > 10, (
+            f"the error is only {fp32_only:.3g}x an fp32-only accumulation "
+            f"bound, so this instruction may now be accumulating a K block in "
+            f"fp32; if so the 2^-14 block envelope is no longer justified and "
+            f"`B._FP8_BLOCK_PRECISION` should go rather than be loosened"
+        )
+
+

+## Generation readiness probe
+
+`/health` only checks that the server processes are alive. To also take a pod out of the Service when its engine cannot run the model (e.g. a hung collective or a GPU fault), point the readiness probe at [`/health_generate`](../serving/online_serving/README.md#generation-readiness-check) and keep `/health` for the liveness probe:
+
+```yaml
+livenessProbe:
+  httpGet:
+    path: /health
+    port: 8000
+  initialDelaySeconds: 60
+  periodSeconds: 10
+readinessProbe:
+  httpGet:
+    path: /health_generate?timeout_s=20
+    port: 8000
+  initialDelaySeconds: 60
+  periodSeconds: 10
+  timeoutSeconds: 30
+```
+
+Set `timeoutSeconds` above the `timeout_s` query parameter (20 s by default); the Kubernetes default of 1 s can be shorter than an idle GPU probe. Don't use `/health_generate` for the liveness probe: it returns 503 while the engine sleeps, so the container would be restarted during a weight sync.
+
 ## Serving with gRPC
 
 vLLM can serve models over gRPC instead of HTTP by passing the `--grpc` flag. This requires the optional gRPC dependencies:

 - `/load` - Server load metrics

+- `/health_generate` - Generation readiness check, see [below](#generation-readiness-check)
+
+### Generation readiness check
+
+`/health` checks that the API server and engine processes are alive. `/health_generate` also checks that every engine rank can run the model right now. It returns 200 when the server can serve generation, and 503 with a JSON body otherwise:
+
+```json
+{"status": "not_ready", "reason": "probe_timeout", "message": "...", "engine_ranks": [1], "timeout_s": 20.0}
+```
+
+| Reason | Meaning |
+| :---- | :---- |
+| `engine_dead` | An engine process has died. |
+| `sleeping` | An engine rank is sleeping or paused, e.g. during a weight sync. |
+| `probe_timeout` | An engine rank did not answer in time. Its busy loop is blocked, e.g. in a hung collective, or a single step is taking longer than the timeout. |
+| `probe_failed` | The GPU probe on an idle engine rank raised an error. |
+
+A busy engine rank is reported ready without extra GPU work. An idle rank runs one dummy forward pass on every worker. For MoE models with data parallelism, idle ranks only check that the engine answers, because a dummy batch outside a DP wave could deadlock.
+
+The `timeout_s` query parameter sets how long to wait for each engine rank before reporting `probe_timeout` (default 20 s), e.g. `/health_generate?timeout_s=10`.
+
+Use `/health_generate` for readiness checks and keep `/health` for liveness checks, so that a sleeping or temporarily slow server is taken out of rotation instead of restarted. `/health_generate` is not authenticated with `--api-key`, like `/health`.
+
+While elastic EP is scaling, the server answers every request, including `/health_generate`, with a 503 and an `{"error": ...}` body instead. The Rust frontend (`VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`) does not serve `/health_generate` yet.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Runtime fault injection for `/health_generate` end-to-end tests.
+
+Loaded into the server via `--worker-extension-cls`. Worker faults are
+triggered through the dev `/collective_rpc` endpoint, which only forwards
+strings.
+"""
+
+from typing import Any
+
+import torch
+
+from vllm.config import VllmConfig
+
+
+def _launch_illegal_memory_access() -> None:
+    import triton
+    import triton.language as tl
+
+    @triton.jit
+    def _oob_store(ptr, offset):
+        tl.store(ptr + offset, 1.0)
+
+    buf = torch.empty(1, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32)
+    _oob_store[(1,)](buf, 1 << 42)
+
+
+class FaultInjectionWorkerExtension:
+    vllm_config: VllmConfig
+    model_runner: Any
+    rank: int
+
+    def _fault_targets_me(self, dp_ranks: str) -> bool:
+        # Dense DP engines keep data_parallel_rank=0; the index is the DP rank.
+        rank = self.vllm_config.parallel_config.data_parallel_index
+        return rank in {int(r) for r in dp_ranks.split(",")}
+
+    def fault_ima_now(self, dp_ranks: str) -> None:
+        """Launch an illegal memory access without synchronizing.
+
+        Models a latent async CUDA fault that has not surfaced yet because
+        nothing synchronized afterwards.
+        """
+        if not self._fault_targets_me(dp_ranks):
+            return
+        _launch_illegal_memory_access()
+
+    def fault_ima_now_on_worker(self, worker_rank: str) -> None:
+        """Like `fault_ima_now`, on one TP/PP worker of the engine."""
+        if self.rank == int(worker_rank):
+            _launch_illegal_memory_access()
+
+    def fault_ima_on_next_forward(self, dp_ranks: str) -> None:
+        """Launch an illegal memory access at the end of the next forward
+        pass, so the fault belongs to the readiness probe's own GPU work."""
+        if not self._fault_targets_me(dp_ranks):
+            return
+
+        def hook(*_):
+            handle.remove()
+            _launch_illegal_memory_access()
+
+        handle = self.model_runner.get_model().register_forward_hook(hook)
+
+    def fault_raise_on_next_forward_on_worker(self, worker_rank: str) -> None:
+        """Raise a Python error after the next forward pass on one worker.
+
+        Unlike a CUDA fault, the engine can keep serving after this.
+        """
+        if self.rank != int(worker_rank):
+            return
+
+        def hook(*_):
+            handle.remove()
+            raise RuntimeError("injected probe failure")
+
+        handle = self.model_runner.get_model().register_forward_hook(hook)
+
+    def fault_dp_mismatched_collective(self, dp_ranks: str) -> None:
+        """Enter a DP all-reduce that the other ranks never join (#36594)."""
+        if not self._fault_targets_me(dp_ranks):
+            return
+        from vllm.distributed.parallel_state import get_dp_group
+
+        t = torch.ones(1, device="cuda")
+        torch.distributed.all_reduce(t, group=get_dp_group().device_group)
+        torch.accelerator.synchronize()

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+import os
+import threading
+import time
+from contextlib import contextmanager, suppress
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import requests
+
+from tests.utils import RemoteOpenAIServer
+
+REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[5]
+
+PROBE_TIMEOUT_S = 5.0
+DETECT_DEADLINE_S = PROBE_TIMEOUT_S + 15.0
+
+
+class ReadyProbeServer:
+    """A vLLM server with fault injection hooks and readiness helpers."""
+
+    def __init__(self, server: RemoteOpenAIServer, model: str):
+        self.server = server
+        self.model = model
+
+    def _health_generate(self) -> requests.Response:
+        return requests.get(
+            self.server.url_for("health_generate"),
+            params={"timeout_s": PROBE_TIMEOUT_S},
+            timeout=30,
+        )
+
+    def status(self, path: str = "/health_generate") -> int | None:
+        """Return the HTTP status, or None if the server is unreachable."""
+        try:
+            if path == "/health_generate":
+                return self._health_generate().status_code
+            return requests.get(
+                self.server.url_for(path.lstrip("/")), timeout=30
+            ).status_code
+        except requests.RequestException:
+            return None
+
+    def ready_body(self) -> dict:
+        resp = self._health_generate()
+        return resp.json() if resp.status_code != 200 else {}
+
+    def wait_until_unready(self) -> dict | None:
+        """Return the first not-ready `/health_generate` body, or None."""
+        start = time.monotonic()
+        while time.monotonic() - start < DETECT_DEADLINE_S:
+            with suppress(requests.RequestException):
+                resp = self._health_generate()
+                if resp.status_code != 200:
+                    return resp.json()
+            time.sleep(0.5)
+        return None
+
+    def stays_ready(self, duration_s: float) -> bool:
+        start = time.monotonic()
+        while time.monotonic() - start < duration_s:
+            if self.status() != 200:
+                return False
+            time.sleep(0.5)
+        return True
+
+    def generate(self, max_tokens: int = 8, dp_rank: int | None = None) -> int:
+        headers = {} if dp_rank is None else {"X-data-parallel-rank": str(dp_rank)}
+        resp = requests.post(
+            self.server.url_for("v1/completions"),
+            json={
+                "model": self.model,
+                "prompt": "Hello",
+                "max_tokens": max_tokens,
+                "ignore_eos": True,
+            },
+            headers=headers,
+            timeout=600,
+        )
+        return resp.status_code
+
+    def generate_in_background(self, max_tokens: int, dp_rank: int | None = None):
+        threading.Thread(
+            target=self._generate_quietly, args=(max_tokens, dp_rank), daemon=True
+        ).start()
+
+    @contextmanager
+    def busy(self, dp_ranks: tuple[int | None, ...] = (None,)):
+        """Keep the given DP ranks continuously busy with requests.
+
+        Yields the status codes of the requests sent (0 for a request that
+        raised), so the caller can check that the load was served.
+        """
+        stop = threading.Event()
+        statuses: list[int] = []
+
+        def loop(dp_rank):
+            while not stop.is_set():
+                try:
+                    statuses.append(self.generate(64, dp_rank))
+                except requests.RequestException:
+                    statuses.append(0)
+
+        threads = [
+            threading.Thread(target=loop, args=(rank,), daemon=True)
+            for rank in dp_ranks
+            for _ in range(4)
+        ]
+        for t in threads:
+            t.start()
+        try:
+            yield statuses
+        finally:
+            stop.set()
+            for t in threads:
+                t.join(timeout=60)
+
+    def _generate_quietly(self, max_tokens: int, dp_rank: int | None) -> None:
+        with suppress(requests.RequestException):
+            self.generate(max_tokens, dp_rank)
+
+    def rpc(self, method: str, *args: str, background: bool = False) -> None:
+        """Call a worker method through the dev `/collective_rpc` endpoint."""
+
+        def call():
+            with suppress(requests.RequestException):
+                requests.post(
+                    self.server.url_for("collective_rpc"),
+                    json={"method": method, "args": list(args)},
+                    timeout=600,
+                )
+
+        if background:
+            threading.Thread(target=call, daemon=True).start()
+        else:
+            call()
+
+
+@contextmanager
+def ready_probe_server(model: str, extra_args: list[str]):
+    env = {
+        "VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE": "1",
+        # The engine processes import the fault injection classes by name.
+        "PYTHONPATH": os.pathsep.join(
+            p for p in (str(REPO_ROOT), os.environ.get("PYTHONPATH")) if p
+        ),
+    }
+    args = [
+        "--enforce-eager",
+        "--load-format",
+        "dummy",
+        "--max-model-len",
+        "512",
+        "--max-num-seqs",
+        "16",
+        "--max-num-batched-tokens",
+        "512",
+        "--kernel-config",
+        '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune": false}',
+        # A module-scoped server and a per-test server can share a GPU.
+        "--gpu-memory-utilization",
+        "0.2",
+        "--worker-extension-cls",
+        f"{__package__}.fault_injection.FaultInjectionWorkerExtension",
+        *extra_args,
+    ]
+    with RemoteOpenAIServer(model, args, env_dict=env) as server:
+        yield ReadyProbeServer(server, model)

+## Qwen4Exp PLE offload
+
+To preload a private pinned PLE table, use the same Engram configuration for
+the daemon and engine.
+
+```bash
+vllm preload --model Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
+    --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true,"dp_shared_memory":false}'
+
+vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next --tensor-parallel-size 4 --load-format ipc_cache \
+    --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true,"dp_shared_memory":false}'
+```
+
+The worker receives the GPU handles and pinned CPU storage descriptors in one
+`get_state` response. It maps and registers each memfd locally, then binds the
+PLE accelerator views to the imported tables. The mapping stays registered
+until the last tensor view releases its storage. The loader's existing
+`fallback` setting applies to the whole model.
+
+Private pinned PLE uses `ipc_cache` with either local GPU sharing backend.

+def _unregister(mapping: mmap.mmap) -> None:
+    # The finalizer holds the mmap until the last tensor view releases its storage.
+    host_unregister(ctypes.addressof(ctypes.c_char.from_buffer(mapping)))
+
+
+@dataclass(slots=True)
+class MemfdStorageEntry:
+    fd: SharedFileDescriptor
+    nbytes: int
+
+    @classmethod
+    def from_storage(cls, source: torch.UntypedStorage) -> StorageRecord:
+        size = source.nbytes()
+        fd = SharedFileDescriptor(os.memfd_create("vllm_weight_cache", os.MFD_CLOEXEC))
+        os.ftruncate(fd.fileno(), size)
+        mapping = mmap.mmap(fd.fileno(), size)
+        tensor = torch.frombuffer(mapping, dtype=torch.uint8)
+        tensor.copy_(storage_bytes(source))
+        return StorageRecord(owner=cls(fd, size), storage=tensor.untyped_storage())
+
+    def rebuild(self, device_index: int, cache: dict | None = None) -> StorageRecord:
+        mapping = mmap.mmap(self.fd.fileno(), self.nbytes)
+        buffer = (ctypes.c_ubyte * self.nbytes).from_buffer(mapping)
+        if not host_register(ctypes.addressof(buffer), self.nbytes):
+            del buffer
+            mapping.close()
+            raise ValueError("Could not register pinned CPU weights")
+        finalizer = weakref.finalize(buffer, _unregister, mapping)
+        finalizer.atexit = False  # type: ignore[misc]
+        tensor = torch.frombuffer(buffer, dtype=torch.uint8)
+        return StorageRecord(owner=tensor, storage=tensor.untyped_storage())
+
+
+def materialize_pinned_cpu_storages(
+    storages: list[torch.UntypedStorage],
+) -> list[StorageRecord]:
+    """Move nonempty pinned CPU storages into memfds and wrap the other storages."""
+    records = []
+    for index in range(len(storages)):
+        storage = storages[index]
+        if storage.device.type == "cpu" and storage.nbytes() and storage.is_pinned():
+            record = MemfdStorageEntry.from_storage(storage)
+            # Release the old pinned allocation before copying the next table.
+            storages[index] = record.storage
+            del storage
+            torch.accelerator.empty_host_cache()
+        else:
+            record = StorageRecord(owner=storage, storage=storage)
+        records.append(record)

@@ -1936,7 +1936,7 @@ guide: |
   - **Rust Frontend**: Selected by default in the command builder. Switch to Python if you encounter unsupported features or compatibility issues.
   - **Model Runner v2**: `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`: Model Runner v2 fully supports this model and can be enabled if needed.
   - **Tool calling**: Without a grammar, K3 sometimes calls a tool with no arguments. The opt-in **Strict tool calls** toggle adds `--tool-strict-level parameter` (vLLM 0.31.0 or newer; the day-0 `kimi-k3` images predate it), which constrains every tool call to a declared tool and to that tool's declared argument names and types, as if each tool had set `strict: true`. On the [Kimi Vendor Verifier](https://github.com/MoonshotAI/Kimi-Vendor-Verifier) Tool Call benchmark (70 samples x 5 epochs, 8x MI355X, single-node TP8, Python frontend) K3 scored 0.851 without the flag and 0.983 with it. The Rust frontend builds its own grammar and was not measured; the limits that follow were checked on the Python frontend. The grammar is not a full schema check, so keep validating arguments on the client and retry. A tool schema it cannot compile, such as a `$ref` into the schema's own `properties` or contradictory bounds, fails the whole request (HTTP 400, or an error in the stream of a streaming request), also for tools that do not set `strict`; `--tool-strict-level function` constrains only the call format and the tool name. With the flag, a `tool_choice="auto"` request that also sets `response_format` can return a tool call instead of the structured answer. The toggle is not offered for prefill/decode disaggregation: Dynamo workers do not accept the flag and constrain tool calls through their own `--dyn-enable-structural-tag`.
-  - **AMD (MI355X / MI350X, CDNA4 gfx950)**: `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2=1` (set above) enables AITER's SiTUv2 a4w4 FlyDSL MoE path on builds that carry vllm-project/vllm#53940 (ROCm nightlies since 2026-09-16). v0.30.0 predates it: there the variable is ignored and the MoE runs the default a16w4 path. Unset it or set `0` for the default a16w4 path. On builds with #53940, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2_A8W4` is a deprecated alias for the same a4w4 path and vLLM removes `AITER_SITUV2_A8W4` at startup while the toggle is on; on v0.30.0 and older, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2_A8W4=1` selects the a8w4 path instead. Do not set `AITER_SITUV2_A8W4=1` by itself: vLLM does not derive its MoE weight layout from that AITER flag (vllm-project/vllm#53954 is open), so the two can disagree and corrupt output without an error.
+  - **AMD (MI355X / MI350X, CDNA4 gfx950)**: the routed experts run on AITER's SiTUv2 FlyDSL MoE kernels, and `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2` selects their activation precision: `a4w4` (MXFP4 activations; the default, also selected by leaving it unset, by `auto` and by the legacy `1` set above), `a8w4` (FP8 activations) or `a16w4` (BF16 activations, also the legacy `0`). The default is 4-bit activations, below the MXFP8 activations the checkpoint was trained with. An A/B of `a4w4` against `a8w4` on 8x MI355X (TP8, FP8 KV cache) found no detectable accuracy difference: OCRBench 0.887 vs 0.893 (n=1000) and Kimi Vendor Verifier Tool Call 0.851 vs 0.866 (n=350), both within sampling noise; `a16w4` was not part of that comparison. The startup log line `Using AITER_MXFP4_BF16 for Kimi-K3 SiTU MXFP4 MoE` names the selected mode; on builds where that line carries no mode, it shows only in the AITER kernel names (for example `afp4_wfp4`). The three modes need v0.31.0 or newer (vllm-project/vllm#58201). v0.30.0 ignores the variable and runs a16w4 unless `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2_A8W4=1` selects a8w4; newer builds no longer read that variable. Do not set `AITER_SITUV2_A8W4` or `AITER_SITUV2_A4W4` directly: vLLM overwrites both at startup to match its own setting.
   - **max-model-len**: Adjust max-model-len for different benchmark scenarios for best performance.
   - **RDMA**: If RDMA is enabled, set `UCX_TLS="rc,cuda_copy"` to make sure KV Cache transfer goes through RDMA.
   - **MNNVL environments** (GB200/GB300 NVL): recommend adding `NCCL_MNNVL_ENABLE=1`, `NCCL_CUMEM_ENABLE=1`, and `NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=1`.

+## Rust raw-JSON gRPC rendering
+
+The experimental Rust frontend can render a raw OpenAI Chat Completions JSON
+request without running inference. Start the Rust render server with
+`vllm-rs render <model> --grpc-port 50051` to enable the `vllm.Render` gRPC
+service alongside its HTTP render endpoints. The gRPC service is disabled
+unless `--grpc-port` is set.
+
+Call `Render.Render` with `api = API_CHAT` and the UTF-8 JSON request in the
+`body` bytes field. Only Chat Completions are supported by this raw RPC;
+Completions, Anthropic Messages, Responses, and an unspecified API are rejected.
+For example, this protobuf text-format request supplies the raw body:
+
+```protobuf
+api: API_CHAT
+body: "{\"model\":\"<model>\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"Hello\"}]}"
+mm_payload: MM_PAYLOAD_TENSORS
+```
+
+Choose returned multimodal data with the **proto `mm_payload` field**:
+
+| Value | Returned media |
+| --- | --- |
+| `MM_PAYLOAD_UNSPECIFIED` (default) | Same as `MM_PAYLOAD_TENSORS`. |
+| `MM_PAYLOAD_TENSORS` | Preprocessed inline tensors, hashes, and placeholder ranges. |
+| `MM_PAYLOAD_NONE` | Hashes and placeholder ranges, without inline tensors. |
+
+The JSON body's `mm_payload` and `return_mm_kwargs` fields do not select the
+gRPC output mode. `MM_PAYLOAD_NONE` is useful for routing on the prompt layout;
+its media cannot be forwarded directly to `Inference.Generate` without tensor
+data. Metadata-only mode is currently available on the Python HTTP render routes
+([#65018](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/65018)). The Rust gRPC
+service rejects unknown enum values. The existing typed `Render.RenderChat` RPC keeps its
+`omit_media_kwargs` boolean unchanged.
+
+The response returns prompt token IDs, an effective structured-output
+constraint, a reasoning gate, and preprocessed media. **It does not yet return
+lowered sampling or stopping parameters**, including temperature, max_tokens,
+stop, bad_words, or n. To preserve the request's generation behavior, supply
+equivalent generation parameters separately when constructing the
+`Inference.Generate` request. Copying only the render response is insufficient;
+for example, a temperature and multiple samples requested in JSON would not be
+preserved by those fields alone. This remaining contract work is tracked in
+[#65503](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/65503).
+
 ## Get Responses prompt token IDs
 
 Use `/v1/responses/render` to get prompt token IDs before choosing a model

@@ -41,6 +41,17 @@ The remaining crates are tooling and infrastructure (`vllm-metrics`, `vllm-traci
 
 8. **Keep compatibility code to real consumers.** Internal Rust APIs can change freely: migrate the callers and delete the old path in the same PR. A compatibility layer on a wire contract needs an actual consumer, such as independently versioned gRPC clients or a rolling upgrade, and stays narrow at the wire boundary.
 
+## Request validation
+
+Define each request invariant once (single source of truth), in the lowest layer that owns its semantics:
+
+- **Wire parsing (`serde`)**: JSON shape, field types, and closed wire enums. HTTP handlers take `Result<Json<T>, JsonRejection>` directly (which extracts `body.<path>` on data errors); do not add `validator` derive macros or duplicate bounds onto DTO structs.
+- **Route boundary (`vllm-server` `validate.rs` / `convert.rs`)**: protocol-only invariants that lower crates do not see (such as `stream_options` requiring `stream`, `top_logprobs` requiring `logprobs`, or route-specific `metadata` limits), lowering-time format conversions, and server-state or per-route policy checks (`model_names.check`, `VLLM_MAX_N_SEQUENCES`). Keep temporary rejections of unimplemented fields isolated in `reject_unsupported_fields`.
+- **Shared domain (`vllm-text` / `vllm-chat`)**: cross-route rules — sampling parameter bounds, `max_tokens >= 1`, `min_tokens <= max_tokens`, logprobs, stop strings (non-empty and `VLLM_MAX_STOP_STRINGS`), token IDs and vocab bounds, `cache_salt`, prompt length and truncation, chat messages, tools, templates, and multimodal limits.
+- **Fault classification and `param`**: `vllm_text::Error::kind()` and `vllm_chat::Error::kind()` classify every variant exhaustively into `ErrorKind::InvalidRequest { param }` or `ErrorKind::Internal`. Report the shared layer's canonical `param` name without per-protocol remapping, and leave `param` as `None` only for cross-field or non-field errors.
+
+Upper stages may call the owner's check early to short-circuit before expensive work such as chat template rendering or outbound media fetches.
+
 ## Python frontend parity
 
 - Match the Python frontend's wire behavior: serialization, omitted fields versus `null`, defaults, error status codes, and SSE frame order. Check the actual output, not the Python source alone.

+@pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not current_platform.is_cuda_alike(), reason="Measures device memory."
+)
+def test_get_top_tokens_holds_one_logits_sized_tensor(default_vllm_config):
+    """The local-argmax path applies soft cap and scale in place: extra
+    logits-sized tensors in every draft step can exceed the torch memory cap
+    of an extensible KV cache."""
+    import types
+
+    vocab_size, hidden_size, num_tokens = 262144, 16, 64
+    lp = LogitsProcessor(vocab_size, scale=2.0, soft_cap=30.0)
+
+    hidden_states = torch.randn(
+        num_tokens, hidden_size, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda"
+    )
+    weight = torch.randn(vocab_size, hidden_size, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+    lm_head = _fake_lm_head(
+        weight,
+        shard_indices=types.SimpleNamespace(
+            num_org_vocab_padding=0, org_vocab_start_index=0
+        ),
+    )
+    # Also warms up the GEMM, whose one-time workspace would count in the peak.
+    expected = torch.nn.functional.linear(hidden_states, weight)
+    expected = torch.tanh(expected / lp.soft_cap) * lp.soft_cap * lp.scale
+
+    torch.accelerator.reset_peak_memory_stats()
+    allocated = torch.accelerator.memory_allocated()
+    top = lp.get_top_tokens(lm_head, hidden_states)
+    peak = torch.accelerator.max_memory_allocated() - allocated
+
+    # The cap ties nearby logits in bf16, so compare the selected values.
+    selected = expected.gather(-1, top.unsqueeze(-1)).squeeze(-1)
+    assert torch.equal(selected, expected.max(dim=-1).values)
+    assert peak < 1.5 * expected.nbytes
+

+    """Extend the open trailing value of the `args` object until it closes.

+    `_inkling_arg_converter` returns a verbatim span of `raw_args`, so while
+    the last member value is open every delta appends to the converted JSON

+def _rotates_off_the_table(op) -> bool:

+def _assert_rotated(got, x, table, positions, what) -> None:
+    """`got` is `x` ([tokens, heads, head_dim]) GPT-J-rotated off the table."""
+    cos, sin = table.double()[positions].chunk(2, dim=-1)
+    cos, sin = cos[:, None], sin[:, None]
+    even, odd = x.double()[..., 0::2], x.double()[..., 1::2]
+    ref = torch.stack([even * cos - odd * sin, odd * cos + even * sin], -1)
+    ref = ref.flatten(-2)
+    # One bf16 rounding of the result, plus the FP32 rounding of the products,
+    # which dominates where the rotated value nearly cancels. A BF16 table is
+    # off by up to 2^-9 of the inputs and fails this.
+    ulp = torch.ldexp(
+        torch.ones_like(ref), torch.frexp(ref.abs().float())[1].double() - 8
+    )
+    slack = 2**-22 * (even.abs() + odd.abs()).repeat_interleave(2, dim=-1)
+    err = ((got.double() - ref).abs() / (ulp + slack)).max().item()

Signed-off-by: rebel-eunji <eunji.lee@rebellions.ai>

@@ -25,6 +25,7 @@ vllm serve <model> --ec-transfer-config '{
 - `ec_role="ec_both"`: the same process offloads to and reloads from the CPU tier.
 - The tier is one mmap region (`/dev/shm/vllm_ec_{instance_id}_dp{dp_rank}.mmap`) shared by every TP/PCP worker of the instance; only TP rank 0 / PCP rank 0 writes on save, since all ranks hold identical encoder output.
 - Entries are keyed by `mm_hash`; `EmbeddingCache` evicts ready+unpinned entries FIFO when space is needed.
+- The runner cache and CPU tier can evict independently. When a scheduled chunk uses a runner-cached output that is missing from the CPU tier, the producer saves the existing tensor again without rerunning the encoder. The scheduler pins the step's CPU loads before reserving blocks for these saves. If no blocks are available, the existing missing-entry behavior still applies.
 - Each batched save/load runs on a pooled CUDA stream; completion is reported to the scheduler once the transfer's end event fires (`ECCPUWorker.build_connector_worker_meta` → `ECCPUScheduler.update_connector_output`), which marks saved entries ready and unpins loaded ones.
 - The region is unlinked from `/dev/shm` in `shutdown()`.

[Perf][GLM-5.3-Flash] KDA: planar short conv for chunked prefill on SM10x (#66884)

Signed-off-by: Bolin Sun <bolins@nvidia.com>
